sentences.zh: 魏知古魏知古，深州陸澤人也。

translations.literal: Wei Zhigu—Wei Zhigu was a native of Luze in Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhigu was a native of Luze in Shen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 性方直，早有才名。

translations.literal: By nature he was upright and square; early on he had a reputation for talent.
translations.idiomatic: Upright by nature, he gained an early reputation for ability.

sentences.zh: 弱冠舉進士，累授著作郎，兼修國史。

translations.literal: At the age of twenty he passed the jinshi examination; he was repeatedly appointed Writer of the Palace Library and concurrently compiled the national history.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed Writer of the Palace Library on successive occasions, and also helped compile the national history.

sentences.zh: 長安中，歴遷鳳閣舍人、衞尉少卿。

translations.literal: During the Chang'an era he was promoted in succession to Attendant of the Phoenix Pavilion and Vice Minister of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an period he rose in turn to Phoenix Pavilion attendant and vice minister of the guard.

sentences.zh: 時睿宗居籓，兼檢校相王府司馬。

translations.literal: At that time, when Emperor Ruizong held a princely fief, he also served concurrently as inspector and marshal of the Prince of Xiang's household.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Ruizong was still a prince in his fief, he also served as acting marshal of the Prince of Xiang's household.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，擢拜吏部侍郎，仍並依舊兼修國史，尋進位銀靑光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shenlong era he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, still retaining his concurrent duty of compiling the national history as before; soon afterward he was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver-Green Insignia.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenlong era he was promoted to vice minister of personnel while continuing to compile the national history; he was soon advanced to grand master of splendid happiness with silver-green insignia.

sentences.zh: 明年，丁母憂去職，服闋授晉州刺史。

translations.literal: The following year he left office on account of mourning for his mother; when the mourning period ended he was appointed prefect of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he left office to mourn his mother; when the mourning period ended he was appointed prefect of Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，以故吏召拜黃門侍郎，兼修國史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, he summoned him as a former subordinate and appointed him Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate, with concurrent duty of compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong came to the throne, he recalled him as a former subordinate and appointed him vice minister of the yellow gate, again with responsibility for the national history.

sentences.zh: 景雲二年，遷右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingyun he was transferred to Regular Cavalier Attendant of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Jingyun era he was transferred to regular cavalier attendant of the right.

sentences.zh: 睿宗女金仙、玉眞二公主入道，有制各造一觀，雖屬季夏盛暑，尚營作不止。

translations.literal: Emperor Ruizong's daughters, the Princesses Jinxian and Yuzhen, entered the religious life; an edict ordered that a monastery be built for each, and though it was the height of late summer heat, construction still did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ruizong's daughters, Princesses Jinxian and Yuzhen, took religious vows; an edict directed that a monastery be built for each, and though it was the sweltering late summer, work on them never stopped.

sentences.zh: 知古上疎諫曰：

translations.literal: Zhigu submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zhigu submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞《穀梁傳》曰：「古之君人者，必時視人之所勤：人勤於力則功築罕，人勤於財則貢賦少，人勤於食則百事廢。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the Guliang Commentary says: "The rulers of antiquity were sure to observe from time to time what the people were laboring at: if the people labored at physical strength, then construction of works was rare; if they labored at wealth, then tribute and levies were few; if they labored at food, then the hundred affairs were neglected."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has heard that the Guliang Commentary says: "Ancient rulers always watched what their people were busy with: when the people wore themselves out with labor, public works were few; when they wore themselves out with taxes, tribute was light; when they wore themselves out with food production, everything else fell into neglect."

sentences.zh: 」《書》曰：「不作無益害有益。

translations.literal: " The Book of Documents says: "Do nothing unprofitable that would harm what is profitable."
translations.idiomatic: " The Book of Documents says: "Do nothing useless that would harm what is useful."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「罔咈百姓以從己之欲。

translations.literal: " It also says: "Do not deceive and oppose the hundred surnames to follow your own desires."
translations.idiomatic: " It also says: "Do not mislead and thwart the people to satisfy your own desires."

sentences.zh: 」《禮》曰：「季夏之月，樹木方盛，無有斬伐，不可興土功以妨農。

translations.literal: " The Rites say: "In the month of late summer, when the trees are in full growth, there must be no cutting down; earthworks must not be undertaken to the detriment of agriculture."
translations.idiomatic: " The Rites say: "In late summer, when the trees are in full leaf, there must be no felling; no earthworks may be started that would interfere with farming."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「季夏行冬令，則風寒不時。

translations.literal: " It also says: "If in late summer the ordinances of winter are carried out, then wind and cold will not come at the proper season."
translations.idiomatic: " It also says: "If winter ordinances are enforced in late summer, wind and cold will come at the wrong season."

sentences.zh: 」《語》曰：「修己以安百姓。

translations.literal: " The Analects say: "Cultivate yourself in order to bring peace to the hundred surnames."
translations.idiomatic: " The Analects say: "Cultivate yourself so as to bring peace to the people."

sentences.zh: 」此皆興化立理之教，爲政養人之本。

translations.literal: " All these are teachings for raising transformation and establishing principle—the foundation of governing and nurturing the people.
translations.idiomatic: " These are all teachings for fostering civilization and establishing order—the very foundation of governing and caring for the people.

sentences.zh: 今陛下爲公主造觀，將樹功德以祈福祐。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty is building monasteries for the princesses, intending to plant merit and virtue to pray for blessings and protection.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is now building monasteries for the princesses, intending to accumulate merit and pray for divine protection.

sentences.zh: 但兩觀之地，皆百姓之宅，卒然迫逼，令其轉移，扶老攜幼，投竄無所，發剔椽瓦，呼嗟道路。

translations.literal: Yet the sites of the two monasteries are all the homes of the common people; suddenly they are pressed and compelled to move, supporting the old and leading the young, fleeing with nowhere to go; rafters and tiles are torn away, and lamentation fills the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Yet both monastery sites stand on common people's homes. Suddenly forced to move, they support the elderly and lead the young, fleeing with nowhere to go; rafters and tiles are stripped away, and cries of distress fill the roads.

sentences.zh: 乖人事，違天時，起無用之作，崇不急之務，群心搖搖，衆口籍籍。

translations.literal: This goes against human affairs, violates the season of Heaven, raises useless works, and exalts tasks that are not urgent; hearts everywhere are unsettled, and mouths everywhere are murmuring.
translations.idiomatic: This runs counter to human affairs and violates the season; useless projects are launched and non-urgent tasks are elevated; hearts are unsettled everywhere, and murmuring fills every mouth.

sentences.zh: 陛下爲人父母，欲何以安之？

translations.literal: Your Majesty is father and mother to the people—how do you intend to bring them peace?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is parent to the people—how do you mean to set their minds at ease?

sentences.zh: 且國有簡冊，君舉必記，動則左史書之，言則右史書之。

translations.literal: Moreover, the state has its records; every act of the ruler is sure to be noted—his movements are written by the historian on the left, his words by the historian on the right.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the state keeps records: every act of the ruler is recorded—his deeds by the left historian, his words by the right.

sentences.zh: 是以非禮勿言，非禮勿動。

translations.literal: Therefore one must not speak what is contrary to ritual, and must not act what is contrary to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: do not speak what is not ritual; do not act what is not ritual.

sentences.zh: 夫如是，則君之所舉，可不愼歟！

translations.literal: If it is so, then what the ruler undertakes—can it fail to be treated with caution!
translations.idiomatic: If that is so, can the ruler's every act fail to demand the utmost caution?

sentences.zh: 微臣備位諫諍，兼秉史筆，書而不法，後嗣何觀？

translations.literal: This humble subject holds a place among remonstrators and also wields the historian's brush; if I record what is not according to law, what will posterity have to look upon?
translations.idiomatic: Your humble subject holds a remonstrator's post and also wields the historian's brush; if I record what is not lawful, what will posterity have to read?

sentences.zh: 臣愚必以爲不可。

translations.literal: This subject, in his foolishness, is certain that it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject is convinced that this cannot be allowed.

sentences.zh: 伏願俯順人欲，仰稽天意，降德音，下明策，速罷功役，收之桑楡。

translations.literal: I bow and wish that Your Majesty would bend to follow the people's desires, look up and examine Heaven's intent, issue a gracious edict, promulgate a clear policy, quickly halt the labor service, and gather the people back to their mulberry trees and elms.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly pray that Your Majesty will heed the people's wishes, align with Heaven's intent, issue a gracious edict and clear policy, halt the labor at once, and let the people return to their homes and fields.

sentences.zh: 疎奏不納。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 頃之，又進諫曰：「臣聞人以君爲天，君以人爲本。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he submitted another remonstrance, saying: "Your subject has heard that the people take the ruler as Heaven, and the ruler takes the people as his foundation."
translations.idiomatic: Before long he submitted another remonstrance: "Your subject has heard that the people regard the ruler as Heaven, and the ruler regards the people as his foundation."

sentences.zh: 人安則政理，本固則邦寧。

translations.literal: When the people are at peace, government is well ordered; when the foundation is firm, the state is secure.
translations.idiomatic: When the people are secure, government is well ordered; when the foundation is firm, the realm is at peace.

sentences.zh: 自陛下翦除兇逆，君臨寶位，蒼生颙颙，以爲朝有新政。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty cut down the violent and rebellious and ascended the precious throne, the common people have looked up eagerly, believing that the court would have a new policy.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty cut down the wicked and took the throne, the people looked up eagerly, expecting a new order at court.

sentences.zh: 今風教頽替，日甚一日，府庫空虚，人力雕弊，造作不息，官員日增。

translations.literal: Now customs and instruction are in decay, worsening day by day; the treasuries are empty, human strength is exhausted and worn, construction never ceases, and officials increase daily.
translations.idiomatic: Now customs and instruction are in decline, worsening by the day; the treasuries are empty, the people exhausted, construction never stops, and officials multiply daily.

sentences.zh: 今諸司試及員外、檢校等官，僅至二千餘人，太府之布帛以殫，太倉之米粟難給。

translations.literal: At present trial appointees and supernumerary and inspector officials in the various bureaus number nearly two thousand or more; the Grand Treasury's cloth and silk are exhausted, and the Grand Granary's grain and millet are hard to supply.
translations.idiomatic: Trial appointees, supernumeraries, and acting inspectors in the various offices now number nearly two thousand; the grand treasury's cloth and silk are exhausted, and the grand granary can scarcely meet demand.

sentences.zh: 又金仙、玉眞等觀造作，咸非急務，臣先奏請停，竟仍未止。

translations.literal: Moreover, the construction of the Jinxian, Yuzhen, and other monasteries is none of it urgent business; your subject earlier memorialized requesting that it stop, yet in the end it still has not ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, work on the Jinxian, Yuzhen, and other monasteries is none of it urgent; I memorialized earlier asking that it stop, yet it still has not.

sentences.zh: 今歳前水後旱，五穀不熟，若至來春，必甚饑饉。

translations.literal: This year there was flood early and drought later; the five grains did not ripen—if it comes to next spring, famine will surely be severe.
translations.idiomatic: This year brought flood early and drought later; the grain did not ripen—come next spring, famine will surely be severe.

sentences.zh: 陛下爲人父母，欲何方以賑恤？

translations.literal: Your Majesty is father and mother to the people—from what source do you intend to provide relief and succor?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is parent to the people—from what will you provide relief?

sentences.zh: 療饑拯溺，須及其時。

translations.literal: Healing famine and rescuing the drowning must be done in their proper season.
translations.idiomatic: Relieving famine and saving the drowning must be done in season.

sentences.zh: 又突厥爲患，其來自久，本無禮儀，焉有誠信。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Turks have long been a scourge; from of old they have had no ritual and decorum—how could there be sincerity and good faith?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Turks have long been a menace; they have never known ritual propriety—how could they be trusted?

sentences.zh: 今雖遣使，來請結婚，豺狼之心，首鼠何定。

translations.literal: Now although they have sent envoys requesting a marriage alliance, a wolf's heart—how can a rat that looks two ways be fixed?
translations.idiomatic: Though they now send envoys to request a marriage alliance, their hearts are wolfish—who can say which way a wavering creature will turn?

sentences.zh: 弱則卑順，強則驕逆。

translations.literal: When weak they are humble and submissive; when strong they are arrogant and rebellious.
translations.idiomatic: When weak they are humble and compliant; when strong they are arrogant and defiant.

sentences.zh: 屬草衰月滿，弓勁馬肥，乘中國饑虚，在和親際會，倘或窺犯亭障，國家何以防之？

translations.literal: It happens that the grass withers and the moon is full, bows are strong and horses fat; seizing China's hunger and weakness at the juncture of the marriage alliance, if perchance they should spy out and violate the border posts—how will the state defend against them?
translations.idiomatic: Now the grass is withering and the moon full, their bows strong and horses fat; seizing China's hunger and weakness at the very moment of the marriage alliance, if they should probe and raid the border—how will the state defend itself?

sentences.zh: 臣所論者，事甚急切，伏願特垂詳察。

translations.literal: What your subject discusses is extremely urgent; I bow and wish that Your Majesty would especially bestow careful examination.
translations.idiomatic: What I discuss is extremely urgent; I humbly beg Your Majesty to give it your closest attention.

sentences.zh: 」睿宗嘉其切直，尋令同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: " Emperor Ruizong praised his forthrightness and directness, and soon had him made Associate Grand Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Ruizong praised his blunt honesty and soon appointed him associate grand councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 玄宗在春宮，又令兼左庶子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong was in the Eastern Palace, he was also ordered to serve concurrently as Left Vice Director of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: While Xuanzong was crown prince, he was also made left vice director of the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷戸部尚書，餘如故。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Minister of Revenue; his other duties remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to minister of revenue; his other duties remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 明年，擢拜侍中。

translations.literal: The following year he was promoted to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 先天元年冬，從上畋獵於渭川，因獻詩諷曰：「嘗聞夏太康，五弟訓禽荒。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Xiantian, he accompanied the emperor on a hunt at the Wei River and presented a poem of admonition, saying: "I have heard that Xia King Taikang—his five younger brothers admonished him for his obsession with birds and the wild."
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the first year of Xiantian he accompanied the emperor hunting on the Wei River and presented an admonitory poem: "I have heard of King Taikang of Xia—his five younger brothers warned him against his obsession with the hunt."

sentences.zh: 我後來冬狩，三驅盛禮張。

translations.literal: Our sovereign later held a winter hunt; the grand ceremony of the three-sided drive was fully arrayed.
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign later held a winter hunt, the grand rite of the three-sided drive in full array.

sentences.zh: 順時鷹隼撃，講事武功揚。

translations.literal: In season hawks and falcons struck; martial affairs were rehearsed and military achievement displayed.
translations.idiomatic: In season hawks and falcons struck; martial exercises were held and military prowess displayed.

sentences.zh: 奔走未及去，翾飛豈暇翔。

translations.literal: Running they had not yet escaped; fluttering in flight, how could they find leisure to soar?
translations.idiomatic: They fled before they could escape; in frantic flight, how could they find time to soar?

sentences.zh: 非熊從渭水，瑞雀想陳倉。

translations.literal: Not a bear came from the Wei River; an auspicious sparrow was thought of at Chencang.
translations.idiomatic: No bear came forth from the Wei River; no auspicious sparrow appeared at Chencang.

sentences.zh: 此欲誠難縱，茲遊不可常。

translations.literal: This desire is truly hard to indulge; this excursion cannot be made a habit.
translations.idiomatic: Such desire is hard indeed to indulge; this sort of outing must not become routine.

sentences.zh: 子雲陳《羽獵》，僖伯諫漁棠。

translations.literal: Yang Xiong presented the "Feather Hunt"; Xibo remonstrated against fishing at Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiong wrote the "Feather Hunt"; Xibo remonstrated against fishing at Tang.

sentences.zh: 得失鑒齊、楚，仁恩念禹、湯。

translations.literal: Gain and loss take Qi and Chu as mirrors; benevolence and grace recall Yu and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Take Qi and Chu as mirrors of gain and loss; look to Yu and Tang for benevolence and grace.

sentences.zh: 邕熙諒在宥，亭毒匪多傷。

translations.literal: Harmonious brightness surely lies in pardoning; nurturing and enveloping should not bring much harm.
translations.idiomatic: Harmony surely lies in mercy; nurturing the realm should not mean much killing.

sentences.zh: 《辛甲》今爲史，《虞箴》遂孔彰。

translations.literal: The "Xin Jia" is now history; the "Yu Admonition" is thereby greatly made manifest.
translations.idiomatic: The "Xin Jia" is now part of history; the "Yu Admonition" shines forth all the more.

sentences.zh: 」手制褒之曰：「夫詩者，誌之所以，寫其心懷，實可諷諭君主。

translations.literal: " The emperor wrote in his own hand to praise him, saying: "Poetry is that by which intent is recorded and the heart's feelings are written out; it can truly admonish and instruct the ruler."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor wrote in his own hand to praise him: "Poetry records intent and expresses the heart; it can truly admonish and instruct the ruler."

sentences.zh: 是故揚雄陳《羽獵》，馬卿賦《上林》，爰自《風雅》，率由茲道。

translations.literal: Therefore Yang Xiong presented the "Feather Hunt," and Sima Xiangru composed the "Shanglin"—from the "Airs and Elegies" onward, all have followed this path.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Yang Xiong wrote the "Feather Hunt" and Sima Xiangru the "Shanglin"—from the "Airs and Elegies" onward, all have followed this path.

sentences.zh: 予頃向温泉，觀省風俗，時因暇景，掩渭而畋，方開一面之羅，式展三驅之禮，躬親校獵，聊以從禽。

translations.literal: I recently went to the hot springs to observe and inspect local customs; taking advantage of a leisure moment, I hunted along the Wei, opening the net on one side and performing the ceremony of the three-sided drive, personally directing the hunt, merely to follow the game.
translations.idiomatic: I recently went to the hot springs to observe local customs; in a moment of leisure I hunted along the Wei, opening the net on one side and performing the three-sided drive, personally directing the hunt merely to follow the game.

sentences.zh: 豈意卿有箴規，輔予不逮，自非款誠夙著，其孰能繼於此耶？

translations.literal: Who would have thought that you would have admonitions and regulations to assist me where I fall short? Unless sincerity and good faith were long manifest, who could follow you in this?
translations.idiomatic: I never expected you to offer such admonition and help me where I fall short—who but one of long-proven sincerity could have done as you have?

sentences.zh: 今賜卿物五十段，用申勸獎。

translations.literal: Now I bestow upon you fifty lengths of goods, to express encouragement and reward.
translations.idiomatic: I now bestow fifty lengths of goods upon you as encouragement and reward.

sentences.zh: 二年，累封梁國公。

translations.literal: In the second year he was enfeoffed in succession as Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was enfeoffed as Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 竇懷貞等將謀逆也，知古獨密奏其事。

translations.literal: When Dou Huai Zhen and others were about to plot rebellion, Zhigu alone secretly memorialized about the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Huai Zhen and others were plotting rebellion, Zhigu alone secretly reported it.

sentences.zh: 及懷貞誅，賜實封二百戸、物五百段。

translations.literal: When Huai Zhen was executed, he was granted two hundred taxable households of substantive fief and five hundred lengths of goods.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai Zhen was executed, he was granted a substantive fief of two hundred households and five hundred lengths of goods.

sentences.zh: 仍以前賞猶薄，又手敕曰：「魏知古去年十月已前，屢申啓沃，毎竭忠誠，姦臣有謀，預奏其兆。

translations.literal: Considering that the previous reward was still meager, the emperor again wrote in his own hand: "Wei Zhigu, before last October, repeatedly offered counsel and nourishment, each time exhausting his loyalty and sincerity; when treacherous ministers had designs, he memorialized in advance about the signs."
translations.idiomatic: Finding the earlier reward still insufficient, the emperor wrote again in his own hand: "Before last October Wei Zhigu repeatedly offered loyal counsel; when treacherous ministers plotted, he reported the signs in advance."

sentences.zh: 事君之節，良有可嘉，可更賜實封一百戸。

translations.literal: His integrity in serving his lord is truly praiseworthy; he may be granted an additional substantive fief of one hundred households."
translations.idiomatic: His loyalty in serving his lord is truly commendable; let him be granted an additional substantive fief of one hundred households."

sentences.zh: 」其年冬，令往東都知吏部尚書事，深以爲稱職，手制曰：「卿以宰臣，往知大選，官人之委，情寄尤切。

translations.literal: " That winter he was ordered to go to the Eastern Capital to act as Minister of Personnel; he was deeply regarded as well suited to the post. The emperor wrote in his own hand: "You, as a chief minister, are going to oversee the great selection; the charge of appointing officials is one to which I am especially committed in heart."
translations.idiomatic: " That winter he was sent to the Eastern Capital to oversee the Ministry of Personnel; he was regarded as thoroughly fit for the role. The emperor wrote: "As a chief minister you go to oversee the great selection of officials—a charge to which I am especially committed."

sentences.zh: 遂能端本革弊，忘私徇公，正色而行，厝心不撓。

translations.literal: You have been able to rectify the root and reform abuses, forget private interest and follow the public good, proceed with stern countenance, and set your heart without wavering.
translations.idiomatic: You have rectified abuses at the root, set aside private interest for the public good, acted with stern integrity, and held firm without wavering.

sentences.zh: 鏡已澈則妍媸必鑒，衡已舉則輕重罔違。

translations.literal: When the mirror is clear, beauty and ugliness are surely discerned; when the balance is raised, light and heavy are never violated.
translations.idiomatic: With a clear mirror, beauty and ugliness are surely seen; with the balance raised, light and heavy are never mistaken.

sentences.zh: 朕遠聞之，益用嘉嘆。

translations.literal: I have heard of this from afar and am all the more moved to praise and sigh.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of this from afar, I am all the more moved to praise you.

sentences.zh: 今賜卿衣裳一副，以示所懷。

translations.literal: Now I bestow upon you a set of robes, to express what is in my heart."
translations.idiomatic: I now bestow a set of robes upon you to express my regard."

sentences.zh: 開元元年，官名改易，改爲黃門監。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaiyuan, when official titles were changed, he was made Director of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaiyuan, when official titles were revised, he became director of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 二年，還京，上屢有顧問，恩意甚厚，尋改紫微令。

translations.literal: In the second year he returned to the capital; the emperor repeatedly consulted him, and his favor was very deep; soon afterward he was made Director of the Purple Forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he returned to the capital; the emperor consulted him repeatedly and showed him great favor; he was soon made director of the purple forbidden palace.

sentences.zh: 姚崇深忌憚之，陰加讒毀，乃除工部尚書，罷知政事。

translations.literal: Yao Chong deeply feared and resented him and secretly slandered him; he was then appointed Minister of Works and removed from participation in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong deeply feared and resented him and secretly slandered him; he was then made minister of works and removed from participation in government.

sentences.zh: 三年卒，時年六十九。

translations.literal: In the third year he died, at the age of sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he died, at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫宋璟聞而嘆曰：「叔向古之遺直，子産古之遺愛，能兼之者，其在魏公。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Song Jing heard of it and sighed, saying: "Shuxiang was the surviving integrity of antiquity; Zichan was the surviving love of antiquity—he who could combine both must have been the Duke of Wei."
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Song Jing heard of it and sighed: "Shuxiang embodied the upright integrity of antiquity; Zichan embodied its benevolent love—who but the Duke of Wei could have combined both?"

sentences.zh: 」贈幽州都督，謚曰忠。

translations.literal: " He was posthumously made Military Commissioner of Youzhou; his posthumous title was Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: " He was posthumously made military commissioner of You Prefecture, with the posthumous title Loyal.

sentences.zh: 知古初爲黃門侍郎，表薦洹水令呂太一、蒲州司功參軍齊璟、前右内率府騎曹參軍柳澤。

translations.literal: When Zhigu was first Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate, he memorialized recommending Lü Taiyi, magistrate of Huanshui; Qi Jing, registrar of merit at Pu Prefecture; and Liu Ze, former cavalry adjutant of the Right Inner Rate Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhigu was first vice minister of the yellow gate, he recommended Lü Taiyi, magistrate of Huanshui; Qi Jing, registrar of merit at Pu Prefecture; and Liu Ze, former cavalry adjutant of the right inner rate office.

sentences.zh: 及知吏部尚書事，又擢用密縣尉宋遙、左補闕袁暉、右補闕封希顏、伊闕尉陳希烈，後咸累居淸要，時論以爲有知人之鑒。

translations.literal: When he oversaw the affairs of the Ministry of Personnel, he further promoted and employed Song Yao, magistrate of Mi County; Yuan Hui, Left Remonstrator; Feng Xiyan, Right Remonstrator; and Chen Xilie, magistrate of Yique—all later rose in succession to pure and important posts, and contemporary opinion held that he had the discernment to know men.
translations.idiomatic: When he oversaw the Ministry of Personnel, he further promoted Song Yao, magistrate of Mi County; Yuan Hui, left remonstrator; Feng Xiyan, right remonstrator; and Chen Xilie, magistrate of Yique—all later rose to important posts, and contemporaries held that he had a true eye for talent.

sentences.zh: 文集七巻。

translations.literal: His collected writings comprise seven juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings comprise seven scrolls.

sentences.zh: 盧懷愼盧懷愼，滑州靈昌人。

translations.literal: Lu Huai Shen—Lu Huai Shen was a native of Lingchang in Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Huai Shen was a native of Lingchang in Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其先家於范陽，爲山東著姓。

translations.literal: His ancestors had their family seat in Fanyang and were a prominent surname of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors were established in Fanyang and were a prominent clan of the eastern provinces.

sentences.zh: 祖悊，爲靈昌令，因徙焉。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ti served as magistrate of Lingchang and moved the family there.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ti served as magistrate of Lingchang and moved the family there.

sentences.zh: 懷愼少淸謹，舉進士，歴監察御史、吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: Huai Shen in youth was pure and careful; he passed the jinshi examination and served in succession as Investigating Censor and Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Huai Shen was pure and careful from youth; he passed the jinshi examination and served in turn as investigating censor and vice director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，遷右御史臺中丞，上疎以陳時政得失。

translations.literal: During the Jinglong era he was transferred to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Right Censorate and submitted memorials setting forth the gains and losses of current policy.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jinglong era he was made vice censor-in-chief of the right censorate and submitted memorials on the strengths and failings of current policy.

sentences.zh: 今略載其三篇。

translations.literal: Here three of his pieces are briefly recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Three of his memorials are recorded here in brief.

sentences.zh: 其一曰：

translations.literal: The first says:
translations.idiomatic: The first reads:

sentences.zh: 臣聞孔子曰：「爲邦百年，可以勝殘去殺。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard Confucius say: "Governing a state for a hundred years, one can overcome cruelty and do away with killing."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has heard Confucius say: "Governing a state for a hundred years, one can overcome cruelty and put an end to killing."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「茍有用我者，期月而已，三年有成。

translations.literal: " He also said: "If someone would employ me, in a single month it would be done; in three years there would be achievement."
translations.idiomatic: " He also said: "If someone would employ me, in a month it would show; in three years there would be achievement."

sentences.zh: 」故《書》云「三載考績」，校其功也。

translations.literal: " Therefore the Book of Documents says, "Examine achievements at the end of three years"—to assess one's accomplishments.
translations.idiomatic: " Hence the Book of Documents says, "Examine achievements at the end of three years"—to assess one's accomplishments.

sentences.zh: 昔子産相鄭，更法令，布刑書，一年而人歌之曰：「取我田疇而伍之，取我衣冠而褚之，孰殺子産，吾其與之！

translations.literal: In former times Zichan served as chief minister of Zheng, revised laws and ordinances, and promulgated the penal code; after one year the people sang of him: "He took our fields and made them into groups of five; he took our robes and caps and stored them away—who will kill Zichan? We will help him!"
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Zichan served as chief minister of Zheng, revised laws, and promulgated the penal code; after one year the people sang: "He took our fields and grouped them in fives; he took our robes and stored them away—who will kill Zichan? We will help!"

sentences.zh: 」二年而人又歌之曰：「我有子弟，子産教之，我有田疇，子産殖之，子産而死，誰其嗣之？

translations.literal: " After two years the people sang again: "We have sons and younger brothers—Zichan teaches them; we have fields—Zichan makes them flourish; if Zichan should die, who will succeed him?"
translations.idiomatic: " After two years they sang again: "We have sons and younger brothers—Zichan teaches them; we have fields—Zichan makes them flourish; if Zichan dies, who will succeed him?"

sentences.zh: 」終有遺愛，流芳史策。

translations.literal: " In the end he left a legacy of love, and his fragrance flows through the historical records.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end he left a legacy of love, and his fame flows through the historical records.

sentences.zh: 子産，賢者也，其爲政尚累年而化成，況其常材乎。

translations.literal: Zichan was a worthy man, yet his governing still required years before transformation was achieved—how much more so for ordinary talent?
translations.idiomatic: Zichan was a worthy man, yet his governing still required years before the people were transformed—how much more so for ordinary talent?

sentences.zh: 臣竊見比來州牧、上佐及兩畿縣令，下車布政，罕終四考。

translations.literal: Your subject has privately observed that in recent times prefects, senior assistants, and magistrates of the two capital districts, upon taking office and promulgating policy, rarely complete four terms of assessment.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has observed that in recent times prefects, senior assistants, and magistrates of the two capital districts rarely complete a full four terms of assessment after taking office.

sentences.zh: 在任多者一二年，少者三五月，遽即遷除，不論課最。

translations.literal: Those in office for the most part serve one or two years, for the least three or five months, then are suddenly transferred and promoted without regard to the results of their assessment.
translations.idiomatic: Most serve one or two years, some only three or five months, then are suddenly transferred without regard to their performance ratings.

sentences.zh: 或有歴時未改，便傾耳而聽，企踵而望，爭求冒進，不顧廉恥。

translations.literal: Some, though their term has not yet expired, already incline their ears to listen and stand on tiptoe to look, striving to advance rashly without regard for integrity and shame.
translations.idiomatic: Some, though their term has not expired, already strain to listen and watch for promotion, scrambling ahead without regard for integrity or shame.

sentences.zh: 亦何暇爲陛下宣風布化，求瘼恤人哉！

translations.literal: How then could they spare time to spread influence and disseminate transformation for Your Majesty, to seek out afflictions and show compassion to the people!
translations.idiomatic: How then could they find time to spread Your Majesty's moral influence, relieve suffering, and care for the people!

sentences.zh: 禮義未能興行，風俗未能齊一，戸口所以流散，倉庫所以空虚，百姓雕弊，日更滋甚，職爲此也。

translations.literal: Rites and righteousness cannot be raised and put into practice, customs cannot be unified—the reason households scatter and treasuries stand empty, the reason the common people are worn and exhausted, growing worse day by day, lies in this.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual and righteousness cannot be established, customs cannot be unified, households disperse, treasuries lie empty, and the people's hardship grows worse daily—all because of this.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this so?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 人知吏之不久，則不從其教；

translations.literal: When the people know that officials will not remain long, they do not follow their instruction;
translations.idiomatic: When the people know officials will not stay long, they ignore their guidance;

sentences.zh: 吏知遷之不遙，又不盡其力，偸安爵祿，但養資望。

translations.literal: when officials know that transfer is not far off, they again do not exhaust their strength, stealing ease in rank and emolument, merely cultivating their reputation and standing.
translations.idiomatic: when officials know promotion is near, they slack off, content to draw salary and build résumés rather than serve wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 陛下雖勤勞之懷，宵衣旰食，然僥幸路啓，上下相蒙，共爲茍且而已，寧盡至公乎？

translations.literal: Although Your Majesty has a mind of diligence and toil, rising before dawn and eating after dark, yet the path of opportunism is opened; superiors and subordinates deceive one another, together making do with the expedient alone—could they exhaust utmost fairness?
translations.idiomatic: Though Your Majesty toils from dawn till dusk, the door to opportunism stands open; officials deceive one another and settle for expediency—how could they truly serve the public good?

sentences.zh: 此國之病也。

translations.literal: This is the sickness of the state.
translations.idiomatic: This is the state's malady.

sentences.zh: 昔賈誼所謂蹠盭之病，乃小小者耳。

translations.literal: The illness of which Jia Yi spoke—the disease of the toenail—was only a small one.
translations.idiomatic: The affliction Jia Yi called a toenail ailment was trivial by comparison.

sentences.zh: 此弊久而不革，臣恐爲膏肓，雖和、緩不能療，豈蹠盭而已哉！

translations.literal: If this evil long goes unreformed, your subject fears it will become an illness in the vital core; even Bian Que and Chunyu Yi could not cure it—how could it be merely a toenail ailment!
translations.idiomatic: If this abuse persists unreformed, I fear it will reach the vital organs—no physician could cure it. Far worse than a toenail ailment!

sentences.zh: 漢宣帝綜核名實，興理致化。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan of Han comprehensively verified names against reality, raised orderly government, and achieved transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan of Han matched names to reality and brought order and moral transformation.

sentences.zh: 黃霸，良二千石也，就增秩賜金，以旌其能，而不遷於潁川，前代之美政也。

translations.literal: Huang Ba was an excellent prefect; they increased his rank and bestowed gold upon him to honor his ability, yet did not transfer him from Yingchuan—a fine policy of former ages.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Ba was an exemplary prefect; the court raised his rank and gave him gold to honor his merit, yet left him in Yingchuan—a fine policy of earlier dynasties.

sentences.zh: 又古之爲吏者長子孫，倉氏、瘐氏，即其後也。

translations.literal: Moreover, ancient men who served as officials had their sons and grandsons succeed them—the clans of Cang and Yu were their descendants.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, officials' sons and grandsons often succeeded them—the Cang and Yu clans are examples.

sentences.zh: 《書》云：「事不師古，以克永代，匪説攸聞。

translations.literal: The Book of Documents says: "If affairs do not take antiquity as teacher, that one may succeed through the ages—such talk has never been heard."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says: "He who does not follow antiquity in governing cannot secure lasting rule—such counsel is unheard of."

sentences.zh: 」臣望請諸州都督、刺史、上佐及兩畿縣令等，在任未經四考已上，不許遷除。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes to request that for regional commanders, prefects, chief administrators, and county magistrates of the two capital circuits and the like, if they have not yet completed four performance reviews in office, transfer and promotion shall not be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that regional commanders, prefects, senior aides, and magistrates of the two capital circuits not be transferred or promoted until they have completed at least four performance reviews.

sentences.zh: 察其課效尤異者，或錫以車裘，或就加祿秩，或降使臨問，並璽書慰勉。

translations.literal: When their assessed achievements are especially outstanding, some may be granted carriages and furs, some may have rank and salary increased on the spot, some may receive imperial envoys sent to inquire in person, together with edicts bearing the seal to comfort and encourage.
translations.idiomatic: Those with outstanding performance might receive carriages and furs, on-the-spot promotions, imperial envoys sent to inquire of them, or edicts of commendation.

sentences.zh: 若公卿有闕，則擢以勸能。

translations.literal: If there are vacancies among ministers and grandees, promote them to encourage merit.
translations.idiomatic: When high offices fall vacant, promote them to reward capable service.

sentences.zh: 其政績無聞及犯貪暴者，免歸田裏。

translations.literal: Those whose administrative achievements are unheard of and those who commit greed and cruelty shall be dismissed and sent back to their fields and villages.
translations.idiomatic: Those who achieve nothing or who are greedy and cruel should be dismissed and sent home to their villages.

sentences.zh: 以明聖朝賞罰之信，則萬方之人，一變於道矣。

translations.literal: By making clear the faith of the sage court in reward and punishment, then the people of the ten thousand directions will all transform as one in the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Make the court's reward and punishment unmistakable, and the people everywhere will reform at once.

sentences.zh: 致此之美，革彼之弊，易於反掌，陛下何惜而不行哉！

translations.literal: To achieve this excellence and reform that evil is as easy as turning the palm—why should Your Majesty be reluctant and not implement it!
translations.idiomatic: Achieving this good and ending that abuse is as easy as turning one's hand—why hesitate to act?

sentences.zh: 其二曰：

translations.literal: The second proposal says:
translations.idiomatic: Second:

sentences.zh: 臣聞《尚書》云：「唐、虞稽古，建官惟百；

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the Book of Documents says: "Tang and Yu examined antiquity and established offices numbering only a hundred;
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says: "Tang and Yu looked to antiquity and established but a hundred offices;

sentences.zh: 夏、商官倍，亦克用乂。

translations.literal: Xia and Shang doubled the offices, yet they were still able to bring order."
translations.idiomatic: Xia and Shang doubled the offices, yet still governed well."

sentences.zh: 」此省官之義也。

translations.literal: This is the principle of reducing officials.
translations.idiomatic: This is the principle of keeping the bureaucracy lean.

sentences.zh: 又云：「官不必備，惟其才。

translations.literal: It also says: "Offices need not all be filled—only seek out talent."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "Posts need not all be filled—only talent matters."

sentences.zh: 」又云：「無曠庶官，天工人其代之。

translations.literal: It also says: "Let no office stand idle—the work of Heaven is performed by men."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "Let no office stand idle—Heaven's work is done by men."

sentences.zh: 」此爲官擇人之義也。

translations.literal: This is the principle of selecting men for offices.
translations.idiomatic: This is the principle of choosing the right people for office.

sentences.zh: 臣竊見京諸司員外官，所在委積，多者數餘十倍，近古以來未之有也。

translations.literal: Your subject has privately observed that supernumerary officials in the various offices of the capital lie piled up everywhere—in some cases numbering more than ten times the regular complement; nothing like this has existed since recent antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that supernumerary officials in the capital's offices lie piled up everywhere—in some bureaus exceeding the regular staff tenfold, unprecedented in recent history.

sentences.zh: 官不必備，此則有餘，人代天工，多不厘務。

translations.literal: "Offices need not all be filled"—here there is surplus; "men perform Heaven's work"—most do not put affairs in order.
translations.idiomatic: Posts need not all be filled, yet here they overflow; Heaven's work should be done by men, yet most perform no duties.

sentences.zh: 廣有除拜，無所裨益，俸祿之費，歳巨億萬，空竭府藏而已，豈致理之基哉！

translations.literal: Broadly conferring appointments without any benefit; the cost of salaries runs to hundreds of millions each year, merely draining the treasury empty—how is this the foundation of achieving good order!
translations.idiomatic: Appointments multiply without purpose; salaries cost hundreds of millions yearly, draining the treasury—how can this be the foundation of good government?

sentences.zh: 方今倉庫空虚，百姓雕弊，河、渭漕輓，西給京師，公私損耗，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: At present the granaries and treasuries are empty, the common people worn and exhausted; transport on the Yellow and Wei rivers supplies the western capital, and public and private losses are beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Granaries stand empty, the people exhausted; grain barged on the Yellow and Wei feeds the capital, and losses public and private are beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 況邊隅未靜，兵革猶興，節用愛人，正在今日，增官廣費，豈曰其時？

translations.literal: Moreover the frontier regions are not yet settled, warfare still arises—frugality and cherishing the people are precisely what is needed today; expanding offices and broadening expense—can this be called timely?
translations.idiomatic: The frontiers are unsettled and war continues—now is the time for frugality and care for the people, not for swelling the bureaucracy and its costs.

sentences.zh: 倘水旱成災，租稅減入，水衡無貫朽之蓄，京瘐闕流衍之儲。

translations.literal: If flood and drought become disasters, land tax revenue decreases—the Directorate of Waters and Parks will have no stores of rotting strings of cash, and the capital granaries will lack overflowing reserves.
translations.idiomatic: Should flood or drought strike and tax revenue fall, the treasury will have no rotting strings of cash, and the capital granaries no surplus.

sentences.zh: 或疆塲外守，兵車遠出；

translations.literal: perhaps defending the frontier abroad, chariots and troops sent far out;
translations.idiomatic: troops may need to defend distant frontiers;

sentences.zh: 或收茂無歳，賑救在辰。

translations.literal: or harvests fail and there is no year's grain, and relief must come in its hour.
translations.idiomatic: or harvests may fail and famine relief become urgent.

sentences.zh: 此軍國之急務也，陛下將何以濟之乎？

translations.literal: These are urgent tasks of army and state—how will Your Majesty meet them?
translations.idiomatic: These are urgent matters of state and army—how will Your Majesty meet them?

sentences.zh: 《書》云：「無輕人事，惟艱；

translations.literal: The Book of Documents says: "Do not treat human affairs lightly—consider their difficulty;
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says: "Do not treat human affairs lightly—think how hard they are;

sentences.zh: 無安厥位，惟危。

translations.literal: do not rest secure in your position—consider its peril."
translations.idiomatic: do not rest secure in your place—think how perilous it is."

sentences.zh: 」又云：「不見是圖。

translations.literal: It also says: "Do not pursue what you do not see clearly."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "Do not pursue what is not clearly right."

sentences.zh: 」此皆愼微之深旨也。

translations.literal: These are all the profound import of vigilance against the minute.
translations.idiomatic: These are profound lessons in vigilance against small beginnings.

sentences.zh: 臣竊見員外官中，或簪裾雅望，或臺閣舊人，或明習憲章，或諳閑政要，皆一時之良幹也。

translations.literal: Your subject has privately observed that among supernumerary officials, some have elegant standing in court dress, some are veterans of the central offices, some are clearly versed in statutes, some are well acquainted with the essentials of governance—all are fine timber of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Among supernumeraries are men of courtly reputation, veterans of the central offices, masters of law, and seasoned administrators—all capable men of their day.

sentences.zh: 多不司案牘，空屍祿俸，滯其才而不申其用，尊其位而不盡其力。

translations.literal: Most do not manage documents and records, empty corpses drawing salary, their talent stagnant and their use unapplied, their rank honored yet their strength not exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Most handle no documents, drawing salary for nothing—their talents wasted, their ranks honored yet their abilities unused.

sentences.zh: 周稱多士，漢曰得人，豈其然歟？

translations.literal: The Zhou praised having many scholars; the Han said they obtained men—is it really so?
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou praised their many worthy men; the Han boasted of finding talent—is this what they meant?

sentences.zh: 必有異於此矣。

translations.literal: Surely it must differ from this.
translations.idiomatic: Surely they meant something quite different.

sentences.zh: 臣望請諸司員外官有才能器識、衆共聞知，堪爲州牧縣宰及上佐者，並請遷擢，使宣力四方，申其智效。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes to request that supernumerary officials in the various bureaus who have ability, talent, and judgment widely known by all, and who are fit to serve as prefects, county magistrates, and chief administrators, all be transferred and promoted, sent to exert their strength in the four directions and apply their wisdom and effectiveness.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that capable supernumeraries known to all be promoted to prefectures and counties, sent forth to serve and prove their worth.

sentences.zh: 有老病及不堪理務者，咸從廢省，使賢不肖較然殊貫。

translations.literal: Those who are aged and ill or unfit to manage affairs should all be eliminated and reduced, so that the worthy and unworthy are clearly distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: The aged, infirm, and incompetent should all be removed, so worthy and unworthy stand clearly apart.

sentences.zh: 此濟時之切務也，安可謂行之艱哉？

translations.literal: This is an urgent task for saving the age—how can one say it is hard to implement?
translations.idiomatic: This is urgent business for the times—surely it cannot be called difficult.

sentences.zh: 其三曰：

translations.literal: The third proposal says:
translations.idiomatic: Third:

sentences.zh: 臣聞天吏逸德，烈於猛火；

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that an official of Heaven who indulges in vice is fiercer than raging fire;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that corrupt officials are fiercer than raging fire;

sentences.zh: 貪人敗類，取興大風。

translations.literal: a greedy man who destroys his kind summons great wind.
translations.idiomatic: greedy men who ruin their kind stir up great storms.

sentences.zh: 則知冒於寵賂，侮於鰥寡，爲政之蠹，莫先於茲。

translations.literal: From this one knows that taking bribes and showing contempt for widowers and widows—these are pests of governance, and nothing comes before this.
translations.idiomatic: Bribery and mistreatment of widows and orphans are the worst cankers of government.

sentences.zh: 臣竊見内外官人，有不率憲章，公犯贓汙，侵牟萬姓，劓割蒸人，鞫按非虚，刑憲已及者，或俄復舊資，雖負殘削之名，還膺牧宰之任，或江、淮、嶺、磧，微示懲貶，而徇財黷貨，罕能悛革，委以共理，俟河之淸。

translations.literal: Your subject has privately observed that among inner and outer officials, some do not follow statutes, openly commit corruption, encroach upon and exploit the myriad people, flay and carve the common folk—investigation and trial are not empty, penal law has already reached them—yet some soon recover their former status; though bearing the name of severe reduction, they again receive the duties of prefect and magistrate; or in the Yangtze, Huai, Ling, and desert regions they receive only slight punishment and demotion, yet pursuing wealth and profiting from office, they rarely reform; entrusting them with joint governance is like waiting for the river to clear.
translations.idiomatic: I see officials who violate the law, rob the people, and are duly convicted—yet some soon recover their former rank and again govern prefectures and counties; others receive only a token demotion to the Yangtze, Huai, Ling, or frontier regions, yet continue their greed and rarely reform. To assign them to govern is to wait for the Yellow River to run clear.

sentences.zh: 臣聞明主之於萬姓也，必暢以平分，而無偏施。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that a wise ruler toward the myriad people must extend even distribution without partial bestowal.
translations.idiomatic: A wise ruler treats all the people with even-handed justice, without favoring some over others.

sentences.zh: 若犯罪之吏，作牧遐方，便是屈法惠姦，恤近遺遠矣。

translations.literal: If criminal officials are made governors of distant regions, this is bending the law to favor the wicked, caring for the near and abandoning the far.
translations.idiomatic: To assign convicted officials to govern distant regions is to bend the law for the wicked—caring for the center and abandoning the periphery.

sentences.zh: 凡左降之人，鮮能省過，必懷自棄，長惡滋深。

translations.literal: Generally those demoted and reduced rarely reform their faults; they must harbor self-abandonment, and their evil grows ever deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Demoted officials rarely reform; they give up on themselves and grow worse.

sentences.zh: 則小州遠郡，蠻陬夷落，何負於聖化，獨受其弊政乎！

translations.literal: Then what have small prefectures, distant commanderies, barbarian corners, and tribal settlements done to deserve the sage transformation, that they alone should suffer misgovernment!
translations.idiomatic: What have remote prefectures and frontier tribes done to deserve the court's reform, that they alone should suffer bad governors!

sentences.zh: 昔孟嘗廉明，方臨合浦；

translations.literal: Formerly Meng Chang was incorrupt and clear when he first arrived at Hepu;
translations.idiomatic: Meng Chang was noted for integrity when he governed Hepu;

sentences.zh: 隱之淸絜，乃蒞番禺。

translations.literal: Yin Zhi was pure and clean when he came to Panyu.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhi was known for purity when he governed Panyu.

sentences.zh: 郅都之鎭靜朔方，耿恭之輯寧疎勒。

translations.literal: Zhi Du pacified Shuofang; Geng Gong brought order to Shule.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Du pacified the northern frontier; Geng Gong restored order at Shule.

sentences.zh: 地則遐僻，必擇賢良，務以寧濟爲懷，豈以遐荒見隔？

translations.literal: Though the land is remote and secluded, one must choose the worthy and good, aiming at peace and relief as one's intent—how could remoteness and wilderness be made a barrier?
translations.idiomatic: Remote lands require the worthy chosen with peace as the aim—distance should not excuse neglect.

sentences.zh: 況邊僥之地，夷夏雜處，負險恃遠，易擾難安，彌藉循良，以寄綏撫。

translations.literal: Moreover frontier borderlands where barbarians and Chinese mix, relying on perilous terrain and distant position, are easily disturbed and hard to pacify—all the more do they rely on upright and good officials to entrust calming and soothing.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier regions where Han and non-Han peoples mix, dangerous and distant, are hard to govern—they depend all the more on upright officials to maintain order.

sentences.zh: 若委失其任，官非其才，淩虐黎庶，侵剝蕃部，小則坐致流亡，大則起爲盜賊。

translations.literal: If one appoints wrongly and the office does not match the talent, oppressing the common people and exploiting frontier tribes, in small matters this will lead to flight, in great matters to rising as bandits and rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Wrong appointments that oppress the people and exploit frontier tribes may drive them to flee—or to rebel.

sentences.zh: 由此言之，不可用凡材，而況於猾吏乎！

translations.literal: From this speaking, ordinary talent cannot be used—how much less cunning officials!
translations.idiomatic: Ordinary men will not suffice—much less corrupt ones!

sentences.zh: 其内外官人有犯贓賄推勘得實者，臣望請削跡簪裾，十數年間不許齒録。

translations.literal: As for inner and outer officials who have committed bribery and whose cases upon investigation prove true, your subject wishes to request that they be stripped of court rank, and for ten or more years not be permitted registration for office.
translations.idiomatic: Officials convicted of bribery should be stripped of rank and barred from office for a decade or more.

sentences.zh: 《書》云：「旌別淑匿，黜陟幽明。

translations.literal: The Book of Documents says: "Mark and distinguish the good and the bad; demote the obscure and promote the bright."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says: "Distinguish the good from the bad; demote the unworthy and promote the worthy."

sentences.zh: 」即其義也。

translations.literal: This is its meaning.
translations.idiomatic: That is the principle.

sentences.zh: 若不循此道，去邪有疑，善政能官，甄獎或未之偏，擔贓負賄，僥幸或即蒙升，則賞罰無章，沮勸安寄？

translations.literal: If this way is not followed, in removing the wicked there is doubt; for good governance and capable officials, selection and reward may fall short and be partial; those bearing corruption and bribes by opportunism may at once receive promotion—then reward and punishment will have no rule; upon what can encouragement and discouragement rely?
translations.idiomatic: Without this policy, the wicked may escape, the worthy go unrewarded, and the corrupt may be promoted by luck—how then can reward and punishment guide conduct?

sentences.zh: 浮競之風轉扇，廉恥之行漸隤，其源不塞，爲蠹斯甚。

translations.literal: The wind of superficial competition turns and fans; conduct of integrity and shame gradually crumbles—if the source is not stopped, the harm as pest will be severe.
translations.idiomatic: Ambition and cynicism spread; integrity erodes—unless the source is cut off, the damage will be grave.

sentences.zh: 疎奏不納。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 累遷黃門侍郎，賜爵漁陽伯。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate and enfeoffed as Baron of Yuyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate and enfeoffed as Baron of Yuyang.

sentences.zh: 先天二年，與侍中魏知古於東都分掌選事，尋征還同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiantian, together with Palace Attendant Wei Zhigu he shared charge of selection affairs at the Eastern Capital; soon he was summoned back and made Concurrent Grand Counselor of the Secretariat and Chancellery at the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: In 713, he and Palace Attendant Wei Zhigu shared responsibility for personnel appointments at the Eastern Capital; soon he was recalled and made a third-rank grand counselor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 開元三年，遷黃門監。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaiyuan he was transferred to Director of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In 715 he was appointed Director of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 懷愼與紫微令姚崇對掌樞密，懷愼自以爲吏道不及崇，毎事皆推讓之，時人謂之「伴食宰相。

translations.literal: Lu Huai Shen and Director of the Palace Secretariat Yao Chong jointly held the keys to state secrets; Huai Shen considered himself inferior to Chong in the ways of administration and on every matter deferred to him—contemporaries called him "the chancellor who keeps company at meals."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Huai Shen and Yao Chong, Director of the Secretariat, shared control of state affairs; Huai Shen judged himself less capable than Chong and deferred to him on every matter—people called him "the dinner-party chancellor."

sentences.zh: 」四年，兼吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he additionally served as Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he also served as Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 其秋，以疾篤，累表乞骸骨，許之。

translations.literal: That autumn, because his illness was grave, he repeatedly memorialized requesting retirement; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, gravely ill, he repeatedly asked to retire; the emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 旬日而卒，贈荊州大都督，謚曰文成。

translations.literal: Within ten days he died; he was posthumously honored as Grand Defender of Jingzhou, with the posthumous title Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died within ten days; posthumously honored as Grand Defender of Jingzhou with the title Wencheng, "Cultured and Accomplished."

sentences.zh: 懷愼臨終遺表曰：

translations.literal: Lu Huai Shen's deathbed testament stated:
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Lu Huai Shen submitted a final memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣素無才識，叨沐恩榮，待罪樞密，頗積年序。

translations.literal: Your subject has been without talent or knowledge, yet unduly received grace and glory, bearing office in the inner secretariat, accumulating years in due course.
translations.idiomatic: I have no real talent, yet have enjoyed imperial favor and served at the heart of government for many years.

sentences.zh: 報國之心，空知自竭；

translations.literal: The heart to repay the state—I know only to exhaust myself in vain;
translations.idiomatic: My wish to serve the state has been sincere, though my ability to do so limited;

sentences.zh: 推賢之誌，終未克申。

translations.literal: the will to recommend the worthy—in the end could not be fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: my wish to recommend worthy men I never fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 孤負明恩，夙夜惶懼。

translations.literal: Having failed the bright grace, morning and night I am filled with fear.
translations.idiomatic: I have failed Your Majesty's grace and live in constant anxiety.

sentences.zh: 臣染疾已久，形神欲離，鳧鴈之飛，未爲之少，而犬馬之誌，終祈上聞，其鳴也哀，乞求聖察。

translations.literal: Your subject has been afflicted with illness for long; body and spirit are about to part—the flight of wild ducks and geese does not shorten it; yet the will of the dog and horse, in the end I pray may reach Your Majesty's hearing; its cry is mournful—I beg for imperial notice.
translations.idiomatic: Long ill, my body and spirit near parting—the geese may fly on, but this old servant's plea I must still raise; hear my mournful cry, I beg Your Majesty's attention.

sentences.zh: 宋璟立性公直，執心貞固，文學足以經務，識略期於佐時，動惟直道，行不茍合，聞諸朝野之説，實爲社稷之臣。

translations.literal: Song Jing by nature is upright and fair, his heart firm and steadfast; his literary learning suffices for managing affairs, his insight and strategy fit for assisting the age; in movement he follows only the straight path, in conduct he does not compromise—heard in the talk of court and countryside, he is truly a minister of the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing is upright by nature, resolute in principle, learned enough for statecraft, and shrewd enough to serve the times; he acts with integrity and never compromises—court and countryside alike call him a pillar of the realm.

sentences.zh: 李傑勤苦絶倫，貞介獨立，公家之事，知無不爲，幹時之材，衆議推許。

translations.literal: Li Jie in diligence and hardship is without peer, upright and independent; in matters of the public house, knowing them he does not fail to act—a talent for serving the age, widely praised and approved in common discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jie is unmatched in diligence, upright and independent; on public business he leaves nothing undone—a man of the times widely praised for his ability.

sentences.zh: 李朝隱操履堅貞，才識通贍，守文奉法，頗懷鐵石之心，事上竭誠，實盡人臣之節。

translations.literal: Li Chaoyin in conduct is firm and steadfast, in talent and knowledge comprehensive and ample; he upholds the written law and follows statutes, bearing a heart rather like iron and stone; in serving his superiors he exhausts sincerity—truly fulfilling a minister's full measure.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chaoyin is steadfast in conduct, broad in talent and learning; he upholds the law with an iron will and serves his sovereign with complete devotion—a true minister in every respect.

sentences.zh: 盧從願淸貞謹愼，理識周密，始終若一，朝野共知，簡要之才，不可多得。

translations.literal: Lu Congyuan is pure, upright, careful, and cautious; in reasoning and knowledge thorough and close; from beginning to end as one—known alike at court and in the countryside; a talent for concision and substance, not easily found in abundance.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Congyuan is pure, careful, and thorough in judgment, consistent from first to last—known throughout court and country as a concise and capable man, rare to find.

sentences.zh: 並明時重器，聖代良臣。

translations.literal: All are heavy vessels of the bright age, fine ministers of the sage dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: All are pillars of the age and worthy ministers of this enlightened reign.

sentences.zh: 比經任使，微有愆失，所坐者小，所棄者大，所累者輕，所貶者遠。

translations.literal: Recently having undergone appointment and service, they had slight faults; what they were charged with was small, what was cast aside was great, what weighed upon them was light, what they were demoted to was distant.
translations.idiomatic: Recently in office they committed minor faults—punished lightly for small offenses, yet cast aside for great service and banished far away.

sentences.zh: 日月雖近，譴責傷深，望垂矜録，漸加進用。

translations.literal: Though the days and months are recent, the censure wounds deeply; I hope Your Majesty will extend pity and record them, gradually advancing and employing them.
translations.idiomatic: Though their demotion was recent, the rebuke cut deep; I beg Your Majesty's compassion to recall them and gradually restore them to office.

sentences.zh: 臣竊聞黃帝所以垂衣裳而天下理者，任風、力也；

translations.literal: Your subject has privately heard that the reason the Yellow Emperor could let his robes hang down and the realm was well ordered was that he employed Feng Hou and Limu;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the Yellow Emperor could govern effortlessly because he employed Feng Hou and Limu;

sentences.zh: 帝堯所以光宅天下者，任稷、祼也。

translations.literal: The reason Emperor Yao brightened and dwelt in the realm was that he employed Hou Ji and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yao brought light to the realm because he employed Hou Ji and Qi.

sentences.zh: 且朝廷者天下之本，賢良者風化之源，得人則庶績其凝，失士則彜倫攸斁。

translations.literal: Moreover the court is the foundation of the realm, the worthy and good are the source of transformation by custom—obtain men and the myriad achievements will be consolidated; lose scholars and constant norms will be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The court is the foundation of the realm, worthy men the source of moral influence—find the right people and all affairs prosper; lose them and order collapses.

sentences.zh: 臣毎見陛下憂勞庶政，勤求理道，愼舉群司，必期稱職，使鹓鷺成列，草澤無遺。

translations.literal: Your subject every time sees Your Majesty anxious and toiling over the myriad affairs of government, diligently seeking the way of good order, carefully elevating the various offices, surely expecting them to fit their posts, causing the court officials to stand in ranks and no talent in grass and marshes to be overlooked.
translations.idiomatic: I see Your Majesty labor over every affair of state, diligently seeking good governance, carefully choosing officials and expecting them to perform—filling the court with talent and leaving none hidden in the wilds.

sentences.zh: 故得歳稔時和，政平訟理，比陛下用賢之明效也。

translations.literal: Therefore harvests are abundant and seasons harmonious, government is level and lawsuits settled—this compares to the bright effect of Your Majesty's employment of the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Hence abundant harvests, harmonious seasons, peaceful government, and settled lawsuits—the clear fruit of Your Majesty's wise use of talent.

sentences.zh: 臣非木石，早識天心，瞑目不遙，厚恩未報。

translations.literal: Your subject is not wood or stone; long ago I knew Heaven's intent; closing my eyes is not far off, yet the deep grace remains unrequited.
translations.idiomatic: I am not made of wood or stone; I have long understood Heaven's will. Death is near, yet Your Majesty's deep grace I have not repaid.

sentences.zh: 黜殯之義，敢不庶幾，城郢之言，思布愚懇。

translations.literal: The principle of remonstrance even at burial—how dare I not hope to approach it; the words spoken at the building of the wall at Ying—I think to spread my humble sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: In the spirit of those who remonstrated even at burial, I dare offer this counsel; as one who would speak plainly before the end, I lay out my humble plea.

sentences.zh: 上深嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor warmly approved the memorial.

sentences.zh: 懷愼淸儉，不營産業，器用服飾，無金玉綺文之麗。

translations.literal: Huai Shen was pure and frugal, not building up estates; utensils, implements, clothing, and adornments had none of the splendor of gold, jade, or brocade patterns.
translations.idiomatic: Huai Shen lived plainly and frugally, building no estate; his furnishings and dress had none of the splendor of gold, jade, or brocade.

sentences.zh: 所得祿俸，皆隨時分散，而家無餘蓄，妻子匱乏。

translations.literal: The salary and emoluments he received were all distributed as occasion arose, and the household had no surplus stores; wife and children were in want.
translations.idiomatic: He gave away his salary as it came in, leaving nothing in reserve; his wife and children lived in want.

sentences.zh: 及車駕將幸東都，四門博士張星上言：「懷愼忠淸直道，終始不虧，不加寵贈，無以勸善。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage was about to visit the Eastern Capital, Erudite of the Four Gates Zhang Xing submitted a statement: "Huai Shen was loyal, pure, and upright in the Way, never failing from beginning to end—if no favor and gift are added, there is no means to encourage goodness."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to visit the Eastern Capital, Erudite Zhang Xing of the Four Gates memorialized: "Huai Shen was loyal, upright, and incorrupt from first to last—without imperial reward, how can virtue be encouraged?"

sentences.zh: 」乃下制賜其家物壹伯段、米粟貳伯石。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued bestowing upon his household one hundred bolts of goods and two hundred shi of grain and millet.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict granting his family one hundred bolts of cloth and two hundred shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 明年，上還京師，因校獵於城南，經懷愼別業，見家人方設祥齋，憫其貧匱，賜絹百匹。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor returned to the capital; while conducting a hunt drill south of the city he passed by Huai Shen's private estate, saw the family holding a mourning feast, took pity on their poverty, and bestowed one hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when the emperor returned to the capital, he went hunting south of the city and passed Lu Huai Shen's country house. Finding the family observing a mourning rite and moved by their poverty, he granted them one hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 仍遣中書侍郎蘇颋爲其碑文，上自書焉。

translations.literal: He further dispatched Vice Director of the Secretariat Su Ting to compose his stele inscription, and the emperor personally wrote it.
translations.idiomatic: He also had Su Ting, Vice Director of the Secretariat, draft the epitaph—and wrote the inscription himself.

sentences.zh: 懷愼子 奐子奐，早修整，歴任皆以淸白聞。

translations.literal: Huai Shen's son Huan—Huan was from youth well ordered and cultivated; in every office he served he was known for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Huai Shen's son Huan was disciplined from an early age, and in every post he held he won renown for spotless conduct.

sentences.zh: 開元中，爲中書舍人、御史中丞、陜州刺史。

translations.literal: During the Kaiyuan era he served as Secretariat Drafter, Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Prefect of Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kaiyuan he rose to Secretariat drafter, vice censor-in-chief, and prefect of Shaan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，玄宗幸京師，次陜城頓，審其能政，於廳事題贊而去，曰：「專城之重，分陜之雄。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year Emperor Xuanzong visited the capital and halted at Shancheng; reviewing Huan's capable administration, he inscribed a commendation in the hall and departed, saying: "The weight of holding a walled city—the might of dividing Shaan."
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 24, when Emperor Xuanzong traveled to the capital and stopped at Shancheng, he inspected Huan's able governance and left an inscription of praise in the prefectural hall: "The burden of a walled prefecture—the strength of the divided Shaan mandate."

sentences.zh: 人多惠愛，性實謙沖。

translations.literal: The people received much of his kindness and love; his nature was truly modest and unassuming.
translations.idiomatic: The people loved him for his kindness, and his character was genuinely humble.

sentences.zh: 亦既利物，在乎匪躬。

translations.literal: He had already benefited things and people; what mattered lay in not keeping to himself.
translations.idiomatic: He had already served the common good; what counted was selfless devotion to duty.

sentences.zh: 斯爲國寶，不墜家風。

translations.literal: This is a treasure of the state; the family tradition does not fall.
translations.idiomatic: Such a man is a national treasure—and the family's reputation remains unblemished.

sentences.zh: 」尋除兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was made vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，爲晉陵太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianbao era he became Prefect of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianbao period he served as prefect of Jinling.

sentences.zh: 時南海郡利兼水陸，環寶山積，劉巨鱗、彭杲相替爲太守、五府節度，皆坐贓鉅萬而死。

translations.literal: At that time Nanhai Commandery profited from both land and water routes, with treasure mountains heaped all around; Liu Julin and Peng Gao alternated as prefect and commissioner of the five prefectures, and both were executed for embezzling tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Nanhai Commandery then offered riches from land and sea trade alike, with hoarded treasure piled high. Liu Julin and Peng Gao had served in turn as prefect and military commissioner of the five prefectures, and both were put to death after amassing fortunes in graft.

sentences.zh: 乃特授奐爲南海太守。

translations.literal: Huan was then specially appointed Prefect of Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Huan was therefore specially appointed prefect of Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 遐方之地，貪吏斂跡，人用安之。

translations.literal: In that distant region greedy officials withdrew their tracks, and the people found peace and security.
translations.idiomatic: In that far southern post, corrupt officials kept their distance, and the people lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 以爲自開元已來四十年，廣府節度淸白者有四：謂宋璟、裴伷先、李朝隱及奐。

translations.literal: It was held that in the forty years since Kaiyuan there had been four incorrupt governors of Guang Prefecture: namely Song Jing, Pei Youxian, Li Chaoyin, and Huan.
translations.idiomatic: People said that in the forty years since Kaiyuan only four governors of Guang Prefecture had remained clean: Song Jing, Pei Youxian, Li Chaoyin, and Huan.

sentences.zh: 中使市舶，亦不幹法。

translations.literal: Even when palace envoys came to trade in maritime goods, he did not bend the law.
translations.idiomatic: Even when imperial envoys came to buy tribute goods from overseas trade, he refused to let them violate the law.

sentences.zh: 加銀靑光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Silver and Blue Gleaming-bright Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Silver-and-Blue Gleaming Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 經三年，入爲尚書右丞，卒。

translations.literal: After three years he entered the capital as Right Vice Director of the Ministry of State Affairs and died.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he was recalled to the capital as right vice director of the Ministry of State Affairs, where he died.

sentences.zh: 弟弈，亦傳淸白，歴御史中丞而死王事，見《忠義傳》。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yi also inherited integrity; he served as Vice Censor-in-Chief and died in service to the state—see the Biographies of Loyalty and Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yi likewise upheld the family's reputation for integrity. He served as vice censor-in-chief and died in the line of duty; his account appears in the Biographies of Loyalty and Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 弈子杞，德宗朝位至宰輔，別有傳。

translations.literal: Yi's son Qi rose to chancellor in the Dezong reign; he has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's son Qi rose to the chancellorship under Emperor Dezong and has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 源乾曜源乾曜，相州臨漳人。

translations.literal: Yuan Qianyao—Yuan Qianyao was a native of Linzhang in Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qianyao was a native of Linzhang in Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 隋比部侍郎師之孫也。

translations.literal: He was the grandson of Shi, Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue under the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: He was the grandson of Shi, vice director of the Sui Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 父直心，髙宗時爲司刑太常伯，坐事配流嶺南而卒。

translations.literal: His father Zhixin served in the Gaozong era as Grand Minister of Justice and of Rites; for an offense he was sentenced to exile in Lingnan, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhixin served under Emperor Gaozong as grand minister of justice and of rites, but after an offense was banished to Lingnan, where he died.

sentences.zh: 乾曜舉進士，景雲中，累遷諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Qianyao passed the jinshi examination; during the Jingyun era he was repeatedly promoted to Remonstrating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyao passed the jinshi examination and, during the Jingyun period, rose in succession to remonstrating censor.

sentences.zh: 時久廢公卿百官三九射禮，乾曜上疎曰：「夫聖王之教天下也，必制禮以正人情，人情正則孝於家，忠於國。

translations.literal: At that time the archery rites of the Three Nines for dukes, ministers, and the hundred officials had long been abandoned; Qianyao submitted a memorial stating: "When a sage king teaches the realm, he must establish ritual to set human feelings right; when human feelings are set right, there is filial piety in the family and loyalty to the state."
translations.idiomatic: The formal archery ceremonies for the court had long fallen into disuse. Qianyao submitted a memorial: "A sage ruler governs by establishing ritual to correct human conduct. When conduct is corrected, filial piety flourishes at home and loyalty in the state."

sentences.zh: 此道不替，所以理也。

translations.literal: When this Way is not replaced, that is why there is good order.
translations.idiomatic: So long as this principle endures, good government follows.

sentences.zh: 所以君子三年不爲禮，禮必壞；

translations.literal: Therefore if for three years the noble man does not perform ritual, ritual must decay;
translations.idiomatic: As the saying goes, if ritual is neglected for three years, it collapses;

sentences.zh: 三年不爲樂，樂必崩。

translations.literal: if for three years he does not perform music, music must crumble.
translations.idiomatic: if music is neglected for three years, it falls apart.

sentences.zh: 竊以古之擇士，先觀射禮，以明和容之義，非取一時之樂。

translations.literal: I venture to think that in antiquity in selecting scholars one first observed the archery rite, to make clear the meaning of harmony and proper bearing—not to take momentary pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, men were chosen for office by first testing them in the archery rite, which taught harmony and proper bearing—not mere sport.

sentences.zh: 夫射者，別正邪，觀德行，中祭祀，辟寇戎。

translations.literal: Archery distinguishes right from wrong, observes virtue and conduct, serves in sacrifices, and repels invaders.
translations.idiomatic: Archery distinguishes right from wrong, reveals character, serves the sacrifices, and prepares men to repel enemies.

sentences.zh: 古先哲王，莫不遞襲。

translations.literal: The sage kings of old none failed to transmit and inherit this in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Every sage king of antiquity handed it down in turn.

sentences.zh: 臣竊見數年已來，射禮便廢，或縁所司惜費，遂令大射有虧。

translations.literal: Your subject has privately seen that in recent years the archery rite has been abandoned, perhaps because the responsible offices begrudged the expense, so that the Great Archery Ceremony has suffered loss.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years I have watched the archery rites fall away, perhaps because the offices responsible begrudged the expense, leaving the Great Archery Ceremony incomplete.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以爲所費者財，所全者禮。

translations.literal: Your foolish subject considers that what is spent is wealth, but what is preserved is ritual.
translations.idiomatic: What is spent is money; what is preserved is ritual itself.

sentences.zh: 故孔子云：『爾愛其羊，我愛其禮。

translations.literal: Therefore Confucius said: "You love the sheep; I love the ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said it plainly: "You care for the sheep; I care for the ritual."

sentences.zh: 』今乾坤再辟，日月貞明，臣望大射之儀，春秋不廢，聖人之教，今古常行，則天下幸甚。
