translations.literal: " Now heaven and earth have opened anew and sun and moon stand firm and bright; your subject hopes the ceremony of the Great Archery may not be abandoned in spring and autumn, that the sage's teaching may run constantly from past to present—then the realm would be greatly blessed.
translations.idiomatic: " Now that the realm has been renewed and the times are bright, I pray that the Great Archery Ceremony may be kept every spring and autumn, so that the sage's teaching endures forever. That would be the realm's good fortune indeed.

sentences.zh: 」乾曜尋出爲梁州都督。

translations.literal: Qianyao was soon sent out as Regional Commander of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Qianyao was posted out as regional commander of Liang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 開元初，邠王府僚吏有犯法者，上令左右求堪爲王府長史者，太常卿姜皎薦乾曜公淸有吏幹，因召見與語。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan a staff member of the Prince of Bin's household had violated the law; the emperor ordered his attendants to seek one fit to serve as chief administrator of the princely household. Minister of Rites Jiang Jiao recommended Qianyao as fair, upright, and possessed of administrative ability, and he was summoned for an audience and conversation.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan, when an official in the household of the Prince of Bin broke the law, the emperor ordered a search for a suitable chief administrator. Minister of Rites Jiang Jiao recommended Qianyao as upright and capable, and the emperor summoned him for an interview.

sentences.zh: 乾曜神氣淸爽，對答皆有倫序，上甚悅之，乃拜少府少監，兼邠王府長史。

translations.literal: Qianyao's spirit and bearing were clear and refreshed; his replies all had proper order; the emperor was greatly pleased and appointed him Vice Director of the Palace Storehouse and concurrently Chief Administrator of the Prince of Bin's household.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyao's manner was clear and alert, and every answer he gave was well ordered. The emperor was greatly pleased and made him vice director of the palace storehouse and chief administrator of the Prince of Bin's household.

sentences.zh: 尋遷戸部侍郎、兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue and concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to vice minister of revenue and vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 無幾，轉尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Ministry of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after he became left vice director of the Ministry of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 四年冬，擢拜黃門侍郎、同紫微黃門平章事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, winter, he was elevated and appointed Vice Director of the Yellow Gate and Associate Director of the Palace Secretariat with the status of Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Kaiyuan 4 he was elevated to vice director of the Yellow Gate and appointed associate grand councillor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 旬日，與姚元之倶罷知政事。

translations.literal: Within ten days he and Yao Yuanzhi were both dismissed from handling state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later he and Yao Yuanzhi were both removed from the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 時行幸東都，以乾曜爲京兆尹，仍京師留守。

translations.literal: At that time, as the emperor traveled to the Eastern Capital, Qianyao was made Governor of Jingzhao and remained as custodian of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled to the Eastern Capital, Qianyao was appointed governor of Jingzhao and left behind as custodian of the capital.

sentences.zh: 乾曜政存寬簡，不嚴而理。

translations.literal: Qianyao's administration preserved leniency and simplicity; without severity there was good order.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyao governed with leniency and restraint, achieving order without harshness.

sentences.zh: 嘗有仗内白鷹，因縱遂失所在，上令京兆切捕之。

translations.literal: Once there was a white hawk from the imperial guard retinue that, having been released, lost its whereabouts; the emperor ordered Jingzhao to hunt it down urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Once a white hunting hawk from the imperial guard escaped and could not be found. The emperor ordered the governor of Jingzhao to capture it at once.

sentences.zh: 俄於野外獲之，其鷹掛於叢棘而死，官吏懼得罪，相顧失色。

translations.literal: Soon it was recovered in the wild, but the hawk had hung upon thorn bushes and died; the officials feared punishment and looked at one another, their faces drained of color.
translations.idiomatic: It was soon found in the countryside, but the bird had caught in a thicket and died. The officials feared punishment and exchanged pale, frightened looks.

sentences.zh: 乾曜徐曰：「事有邂逅，死亦常理，主上仁明，當不以此置罪。

translations.literal: Qianyao said slowly: "Matters have chance encounters; death is also the constant principle. Our lord is benevolent and clear-sighted—he surely will not fix blame for this."
translations.idiomatic: Qianyao said calmly, "Accidents happen, and death is only natural. Our lord is benevolent and wise; he will not punish us for this."

sentences.zh: 必其獲戾，吾自當之，不須懼也。

translations.literal: If blame must be incurred, I myself will bear it—there is no need for fear.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone is to be blamed, I alone will answer for it. There is no need to be afraid.

sentences.zh: 」遂入自請失旨之罪，上一切不問之，衆咸伏乾曜臨事不懾，而能引過在己也。

translations.literal: He then entered and personally requested punishment for failing the imperial intent; the emperor asked nothing about any of it. All admired that Qianyao, facing affairs without fear, could take fault upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: He then went in and asked to be punished for the failure. The emperor dismissed the matter entirely. Everyone admired Qianyao for facing the crisis without flinching and taking responsibility upon himself.

sentences.zh: 在京兆三年，政令如一。

translations.literal: During three years in Jingzhao his government and orders were uniform throughout.
translations.idiomatic: Through three years as governor of Jingzhao, his administration remained steady and consistent.

sentences.zh: 八年春，復爲黃門侍郎、同中書門下三品，尋加銀靑光祿大夫，遷侍中。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year he again became Vice Director of the Yellow Gate and Associate of the Three Departments with the Third Rank; soon he was further made Silver and Blue Gleaming-bright Grand Master and transferred to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Kaiyuan 8 he returned to the chancellorship as vice director of the Yellow Gate and associate of the Three Departments, was soon promoted to Silver-and-Blue Gleaming Grand Master, and then became palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 久之，上疎曰：「臣竊見形要之家並求京職，俊乂之士多任外官，王道平分，不合如此。

translations.literal: After some time he submitted a memorial stating: "Your subject has privately seen that influential families all seek capital appointments, while able and virtuous men mostly hold outer offices—the kingly Way should be evenly divided; it should not be thus."
translations.idiomatic: Before long he submitted a memorial: "I observe that powerful families all seek posts in the capital, while able men are mostly sent to the provinces. The kingly Way demands fairness, and this should not continue."

sentences.zh: 臣三男倶是京任，望出二人與外官，以葉均平之道。

translations.literal: Your subject's three sons are all in capital appointments; I hope to send two of them to outer offices, to accord with the Way of even balance.
translations.idiomatic: All three of my sons hold posts in the capital. I ask that two of them be sent to provincial offices, so that I may practice the fairness I preach.

sentences.zh: 」上從之，於是改其子河南府參軍弼爲絳州司功，太祝絜爲鄭尉。

translations.literal: The emperor assented; thereupon his son Bi, Army Aide of Henan Prefecture, was changed to Merit Officer of Jiang Prefecture, and Jie, Grand Sacrificer, was made Captain of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed. Bi, his son and army aide of Henan Prefecture, was reassigned as merit officer in Jiang Prefecture, and Jie, grand sacrificer, was made captain in Zheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 因下制曰：「源弼等父在樞近，深惟謙挹，恐代官之咸列，慮時才之未序，率先庶僚，崇是讓德，既請外其職，復降資以授。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued stating: "Yuan Bi and the others—their father stands near the pivot of power and deeply considers humility and restraint, fearing that successive offices all stand in rank and worrying that timely talent is not properly ordered; he takes the lead among the multitude of officials and exalts this virtue of yielding; having already requested outer appointments for them, he further accepts reduced rank in their assignment."
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: "Yuan Bi and the others—their father holds a post at the heart of government yet remains deeply modest. Fearing that one family might monopolize office after office, and anxious lest able men go unrewarded, he has led the officials by example in the virtue of yielding. He asked that his sons be sent abroad—and accepted lower rank for them as well."

sentences.zh: 《傳》不云乎：『晉範宣子讓，其下皆讓。

translations.literal: Does not the Commentary say: "When Fan Xuanzi of Jin yielded, those below him all yielded."
translations.idiomatic: Does not the Commentary say, "When Fan Xuanzi of Jin yielded, all beneath him yielded as well"?

sentences.zh: 』『晉國之人，於是大和。

translations.literal: " "The people of the state of Jin then achieved great harmony."
translations.idiomatic: " "And the people of Jin were greatly reconciled."

sentences.zh: 』道之或行，仁豈云遠！

translations.literal: When the Way may thus be put into practice, can benevolence be said to be far away!
translations.idiomatic: When the Way can be practiced like this, how far can benevolence be?

sentences.zh: 」因令文武百僚父子兄弟三人並任京司者，任自通容，依資次處分，由是公卿子弟京官出外者百餘人。

translations.literal: Thereupon civil and military officials of the hundred ranks whose fathers, sons, and brothers—three persons—were all serving in capital offices were ordered, at their own discretion in accordance with suitability, to be assigned according to seniority and qualification; thereby more than a hundred sons of dukes and ministers in capital posts were sent to outer offices.
translations.idiomatic: Officials throughout the court whose fathers, sons, and brothers—three men together—all held capital posts were told to arrange transfers according to rank and qualification. More than a hundred sons of high ministers were sent out from the capital as a result.

sentences.zh: 俄又有上書者，以爲「國之執政，同其休戚，若不稍加崇寵，何以責其盡心？

translations.literal: Soon there was another memorial stating: "Those who hold power in the state share its joys and sorrows; if they are not given some additional honor and favor, how can they be charged to give their full hearts?"
translations.idiomatic: Soon another memorial argued that "the men who govern the state share its fortunes and misfortunes. If they receive no special reward, how can they be expected to serve with full devotion?"

sentences.zh: 」十年十一月，敕中書門下共食實封三百戸，自乾曜及張嘉貞始也。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the tenth year an edict granted the Secretariat and Chancellery together three hundred households of actual enfeoffment; this began with Qianyao and Zhang Jiazhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Kaiyuan 10, an edict granted the Secretariat and Chancellery a combined three hundred taxable households as enfeoffment income—the first such grant, beginning with Qianyao and Zhang Jiazhen.

sentences.zh: 乾曜後扈從東封，拜尚書左丞相，仍兼侍中。

translations.literal: Qianyao later accompanied the emperor on the eastern Feng and Shan rites and was appointed Left Director of the Ministry of State Affairs, still concurrently Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyao later accompanied the emperor on the eastern feng and shan rites and was appointed left director of the Ministry of State Affairs while retaining his post as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 乾曜在政事十年，時張嘉貞、張説相次爲中書令，乾曜不敢與之爭權，毎事皆推讓之。

translations.literal: Qianyao was in state affairs for ten years; at that time Zhang Jiazhen and Zhang Yue successively served as Director of the Secretariat; Qianyao did not dare contend with them for power and on every matter deferred to them.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyao spent ten years in the chancellorship. Zhang Jiazhen and Zhang Yue served in succession as director of the Secretariat, and Qianyao never contested their authority, deferring to them on every matter.

sentences.zh: 及李元纮、杜暹知政事，乾曜遂無所參議，但唯諾署名而已。

translations.literal: When Li Yuanhong and Du Xian handled state affairs, Qianyao then had no part in deliberation and merely assented and signed his name.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yuanhong and Du Xian joined the chancellorship, Qianyao ceased to participate in deliberations and merely nodded assent and signed documents.

sentences.zh: 初，乾曜因姜皎所薦，遂擢用；

translations.literal: At first Qianyao, through Jiang Jiao's recommendation, was then elevated and employed;
translations.idiomatic: Qianyao had first risen through Jiang Jiao's recommendation;

sentences.zh: 及皎得罪，爲張嘉貞所擠，乾曜竟不救之，議者以此譏焉。

translations.literal: when Jiang Jiao incurred guilt and was squeezed out by Zhang Jiazhen, Qianyao in the end did not rescue him—commentators for this reason criticized him.
translations.idiomatic: but when Jiang Jiao fell from favor and was driven out by Zhang Jiazhen, Qianyao never came to his aid. Critics held this against him.

sentences.zh: 十七年夏，停兼侍中事。

translations.literal: In the summer of the seventeenth year he ceased concurrently serving as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Kaiyuan 17 he was relieved of his concurrent post as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 其秋，遷太子少師，以祖名師，固辭，乃拜太子少傅，封安陽郡公。

translations.literal: That autumn he was transferred to Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent; because his grandfather's name was Shi, he firmly declined, and was then appointed Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and enfeoffed as Duke of Anyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was appointed junior preceptor to the heir apparent, but because his grandfather's given name was Shi, he declined the post and was instead made junior tutor to the heir apparent and enfeoffed as Duke of Anyang.

sentences.zh: 十九年，駕幸東都，乾曜以年老辭疾，不堪扈從，因留京養疾。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, when the imperial carriage visited the Eastern Capital, Qianyao, citing old age, pleaded illness and could not bear to accompany the retinue; he therefore remained in the capital to nurse his illness.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 19, when the emperor traveled to the Eastern Capital, Qianyao pleaded old age and illness and was unable to accompany the court. He remained in the capital to recover.

sentences.zh: 是年冬卒，詔贈幽州大都督，上於洛城南門舉哀，輟朝二日。

translations.literal: That winter he died; an edict posthumously granted him the post of Great Regional Commander of Youzhou; the emperor held mourning at the south gate of Luoyang and suspended court for two days.
translations.idiomatic: He died that winter. An edict posthumously granted him the title of great regional commander of You Prefecture. The emperor mourned him at the south gate of Luoyang and suspended court for two days.

sentences.zh: 乾曜從孫 光裕乾曜從孫光裕，亦有令譽。

translations.literal: Qianyao's grandnephew Guangyu—Guangyu also had a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyao's grandnephew Guangyu likewise enjoyed an excellent reputation.

sentences.zh: 歴職淸謹，撫諸弟以友義聞。

translations.literal: In successive offices he was pure and careful; in treating his younger brothers he was known for brotherly righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he served with integrity and discretion, and was known for treating his younger brothers with fraternal devotion.

sentences.zh: 初爲中書舍人，與楊滔、劉令植等同刪定《開元新格》。

translations.literal: At first he served as Secretariat Drafter and, together with Yang Tao, Liu Lingzhi, and others, revised and finalized the New Statutes of Kaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as a secretariat drafter and, with Yang Tao, Liu Lingzhi, and others, helped revise the New Statutes of Kaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 歴刑部戸部二侍郎、尚書左丞，累遷鄭州刺史，稱爲良吏。

translations.literal: He served successively as Vice Minister of Justice and of Revenue and as Left Vice Director of the Ministry of State Affairs; he was repeatedly promoted to Prefect of Zhengzhou and was called a good official.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the vice ministries of justice and revenue to left vice director of the Ministry of State Affairs, then became prefect of Zheng Prefecture, where he was praised as an able administrator.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 光裕子 洧光裕子洧，亦早有美稱。

translations.literal: Guangyu's son Wei—Wei also early had a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyu's son Wei likewise won early praise.

sentences.zh: 閨門雍睦，士友推之，歴踐淸要。

translations.literal: Within his household there was harmony; scholar-friends praised him; he successively held pure and important posts.
translations.idiomatic: His household was harmonious, his peers respected him, and he rose through a series of prestigious offices.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，爲給事中、蔸鄭州刺史、襄州刺史、本道采訪使。

translations.literal: During the Tianbao era he served as Supervising Censor, concurrently Prefect of Zhengzhou, Prefect of Xiangzhou, and Regional Investigating Commissioner of his circuit.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianbao he served as supervising censor, concurrently as prefect of Zheng and Xiang Prefectures, and as regional investigating commissioner of his circuit.

sentences.zh: 及安祿山反，既犯東京，乃以洧爲江陵郡大都督府長史、本道采訪防禦使、攝御史中丞，以兵部郎中徐浩爲襄州刺史、本州防禦守捉使以禦之。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled and had already invaded the Eastern Capital, Wei was then made Chief Administrator of the Great Regional Commandery of Jiangling, Regional Investigating and Defense Commissioner of his circuit, and Acting Vice Censor-in-Chief; Xu Hao, Bureau Director of the Ministry of War, was made Prefect of Xiangzhou and Defense and Guard Commissioner of that prefecture to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled and seized the Eastern Capital, Wei was appointed chief administrator of the Jiangling commandery, regional investigating and defense commissioner, and acting vice censor-in-chief. Xu Hao, bureau director in the Ministry of War, was made prefect of Xiang Prefecture and defense commissioner to hold the line against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 洧至鎭卒。

translations.literal: When Wei reached his post he died.
translations.idiomatic: Wei died soon after reaching his post.

sentences.zh: 李元紘李元紘，其先滑州人，世居京兆之萬年。

translations.literal: Li Yuanhong—Li Yuanhong's ancestors were natives of Huazhou and for generations dwelt in Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuanhong's family originally came from Hua Prefecture and had long lived in Wannian, in the Jingzhao region.

sentences.zh: 本姓丙氏。

translations.literal: Their original surname was the Bing clan.
translations.idiomatic: The clan's original surname was Bing.

sentences.zh: 曾祖粲，隋大業中屯衞大將軍。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Can served in the Daye era of the Sui as General of the Garrison Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Can served under the Sui as a general of the garrison guard during the Daye reign.

sentences.zh: 屬關中賊起，煬帝令粲往京城以西二十四郡逐捕盜賊，粲撫循士衆，甚得其心。

translations.literal: When bandits rose in Guanzhong, Emperor Yang ordered Can to go to the twenty-four commanderies west of the capital to pursue and capture robbers; Can comforted and guided soldiers and masses and greatly won their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels broke out in the Guanzhong region, Emperor Yang sent Can to hunt bandits across the twenty-four commanderies west of the capital. Can treated his troops with care and won their deep loyalty.

sentences.zh: 及義旗入關，粲率其衆歸附，拜宗正卿，封應國公，賜姓李氏。

translations.literal: When the banner of righteousness entered the pass, Can led his followers to submit; he was appointed Director of the Imperial Clan, enfeoffed as Duke of Ying State, and granted the surname Li.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel armies entered the pass, Can led his men over to their side. He was appointed director of the imperial clan, enfeoffed as Duke of Ying, and granted the imperial surname Li.

sentences.zh: 髙祖與之有舊，特蒙恩禮，遷爲左監門大將軍，以年老特令乘馬於宮中檢校。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu had old ties with him and specially received his grace and courtesy; he was transferred to Left General of the Gate Guard; because of old age he was specially permitted to ride a horse within the palace on inspection duty.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu knew him from earlier days and treated him with special favor. He was promoted to left general of the gate guard and, because of his age, was uniquely allowed to ride a horse while inspecting the palace grounds.

sentences.zh: 年八十餘卒，謚曰明。

translations.literal: At over eighty years of age he died; his posthumous title was Ming.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his eighties and was posthumously titled Ming.

sentences.zh: 祖寬，髙宗時爲太常卿，別封隴西郡公。

translations.literal: His grandfather Kuan served under Emperor Gaozong as Minister of Rites and was separately enfeoffed as Duke of Longxi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Kuan served under Emperor Gaozong as minister of rites and was separately enfeoffed as Duke of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 父道廣，則天時爲汴州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Daoguang served in the Wu Zetian era as Prefect of Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Daoguang served under Empress Wu as prefect of Bian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時屬突厥及契丹寇陷河北，兼發河南諸州兵募，百姓騷擾。

translations.literal: At that time the Turks and Khitans raided and captured Hebei; concurrently troops were levied from the various prefectures of Henan, and the common people were thrown into turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Turks and Khitans were ravaging Hebei, and conscription was ordered across the Henan prefectures, throwing the people into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 道廣寬猛折衷，稱爲善政，存收慰撫，汴州獨不逃散。

translations.literal: Daoguang balanced leniency and severity; his administration was called good; through preservation, collection, consolation, and soothing, Bianzhou alone did not see flight and dispersal.
translations.idiomatic: Daoguang tempered severity with mercy and was praised for good governance. Through careful relief and reassurance, Bian Prefecture alone saw no mass flight.

sentences.zh: 尋入爲殿中監、同鳳閣鸞臺平章事，累封金城縣侯。

translations.literal: Soon he entered the capital as Director of the Palace Domestic Service and Associate of the Phoenix Pavilion and Orchid Terrace with the status of Grand Councillor; he was repeatedly enfeoffed as Marquis of Jincheng County.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as director of the palace domestic service and appointed associate grand councillor, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈秦州都督，謚曰成。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was granted Regional Commander of Qinzhou; his posthumous title was Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made regional commander of Qin Prefecture, with the posthumous title Cheng.

sentences.zh: 元紘少謹厚。

translations.literal: Yuanhong from youth was careful and solid.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhong was careful and steadfast from youth.

sentences.zh: 初爲涇州司兵，累遷雍州司戸。

translations.literal: At first he served as Army Aide of Jing Prefecture and was repeatedly promoted to Registrar of Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as army aide in Jing Prefecture and rose in turn to registrar of Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時太平公主與僧寺爭碾硙，公主方承恩用事，百司皆希其旨意，元紘遂斷還僧寺。

translations.literal: At that time Princess Taiping disputed with a Buddhist monastery over a water mill; the princess was then receiving favor and wielding power, and the hundred offices all sought her intent—Yuanhong thereupon judged the case and returned it to the monastery.
translations.idiomatic: When Princess Taiping disputed a water mill with a Buddhist monastery, the princess was then in favor and in power, and every office sought to please her. Yuanhong ruled in the monastery's favor.

sentences.zh: 竇懷貞爲雍州長史，大懼太平勢，促令元紘改斷，元紘大署判後曰：「南山或可改移，此判終無搖動。

translations.literal: Dou Huaizhen was Chief Administrator of Yong Prefecture and greatly feared Princess Taiping's power; he pressed Yuanhong to change the judgment. Yuanhong wrote in large characters after the verdict: "The southern mountains may perhaps be moved; this judgment will never be shaken."
translations.idiomatic: Dou Huaizhen, chief administrator of Yong Prefecture, feared the princess's power and pressed Yuanhong to reverse the ruling. Yuanhong wrote boldly on the judgment: "The southern mountains may be moved, but this verdict will not."

sentences.zh: 」竟執正不撓，懷貞不能奪之。

translations.literal: In the end he upheld rectitude without bending, and Huaizhen could not overturn it.
translations.idiomatic: He held to his ruling without yielding, and Huaizhen could not make him change it.

sentences.zh: 俄轉好畤令，遷潤州司馬，所歴咸有聲績。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Magistrate of Haoqi and promoted to Vice Administrator of Run Prefecture; in every post he had reputation and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made magistrate of Haoqi and then vice administrator of Run Prefecture, earning distinction in every post he held.

sentences.zh: 開元初，三遷萬年縣令，賦役平允，不嚴而理。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, after three promotions he became Magistrate of Wannian County; levies and corvée were fair and even, and without severity there was good order.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan, after three promotions he became magistrate of Wannian County, where taxes and labor service were assessed fairly and order was kept without harshness.

sentences.zh: 俄擢爲京兆尹，尋有詔令元紘疎決三輔。

translations.literal: Soon he was elevated to Governor of Jingzhao; shortly afterward there was an edict ordering Yuanhong to review and decide cases in the Three Adjuncts.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to governor of Jingzhao, and an edict soon followed appointing him to hear and decide cases across the Three Adjuncts.

sentences.zh: 諸王公權要之家，皆縁渠立硙，以害水田，元紘令吏人一切毀之，百姓大獲其利。

translations.literal: Princes, nobles, and powerful households all built mills along the canals, harming the irrigated paddies. Yuanhong ordered his officers to destroy them all, and the common people gained greatly thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Princes, nobles, and the powerful had built mills along the canals, choking off the irrigated fields. Yuanhong ordered his officers to tear them all down, and the people reaped a great benefit.

sentences.zh: 又歴工部、兵部、吏部三侍郎。

translations.literal: He also served in succession as Vice Minister of the Works, Vice Minister of War, and Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to hold the vice ministerships of Works, War, and Personnel in turn.

sentences.zh: 十三年，戸部侍郎楊易、白知愼坐支度失所，皆出爲刺史。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Vice Ministers of Revenue Yang Yi and Bai Zhishèn were convicted of mismanaging expenditures and were both sent out as prefectural governors.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, Vice Ministers of Revenue Yang Yi and Bai Zhishèn were demoted for botching fiscal administration and were both sent out to serve as prefects.

sentences.zh: 上令宰臣及公卿已下精擇堪爲戸部者，多有薦元紘者，將授以戸部尚書，時執政以其資淺，未宜超授，加中大夫，拜戸部侍郎。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the chief ministers and all officials down through the ranks to carefully select someone fit for the Revenue Ministry. Many recommended Yuanhong, and he was about to be appointed Minister of Revenue, but those in power considered his seniority too shallow for such a leap in rank; he was instead promoted to Senior Mentor of the Palace and appointed Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the chief ministers and all officials to choose carefully who should head the Revenue Ministry. Many recommended Yuanhong, and he was nearly made minister, but the men in power judged his standing too slight for so great a promotion. He was given the rank of Senior Mentor of the Palace and appointed vice minister instead.

sentences.zh: 元紘因條奏人間利害及時政得失以奏之，上大悅，因賜衣一副、絹二百匹。

translations.literal: Yuanhong thereupon submitted itemized memorials on benefits and harms to the people and gains and losses in current policy. The emperor was greatly pleased and awarded him one set of garments and two hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhong followed with a detailed memorial on what helped or harmed the people and what was right or wrong in current policy. The emperor was delighted and gave him a suit of clothes and two hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 明年，擢拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: The next year he was elevated and appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and co-signer of Secretariat-Chancellery documents.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat and made a co-signer of Secretariat-Chancellery documents.

sentences.zh: 頃之，加銀靑光祿大夫，賜爵淸水男。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was further granted the rank of Silver-Green Glorious Grand Mentor and enfeoffed as Baron of Qingshui.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was also made Silver-Green Glorious Grand Mentor and enfeoffed as Baron of Qingshui.

sentences.zh: 元紘性淸儉。

translations.literal: Yuanhong was by nature pure and frugal.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhong was by nature upright and austere.

sentences.zh: 既知政事，稍抑奔競之路，務進者頗憚之。

translations.literal: Once he took charge of state affairs, he gradually closed off the path of frantic competition for advancement, and those intent on getting ahead greatly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Once he entered the administration, he began to choke off the scramble for promotion, and the ambitious grew wary of him.

sentences.zh: 時初廢京司職田，議者請於關輔置屯，以實倉稟。

translations.literal: At that time the official allotment fields of the capital offices had just been abolished, and debaters proposed establishing military colonies in the Guanzhong region to fill the granaries.
translations.idiomatic: The capital offices' allotment fields had just been abolished, and some proposed establishing military colonies in the Guanzhong heartland to fill the state granaries.

sentences.zh: 元紘建議曰：「軍國不同，中外異制。

translations.literal: Yuanhong proposed, saying: "The military realm and the civil realm differ; the interior and the frontier follow different systems.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhong argued: "Military affairs and civil government are not the same, and the interior and the frontier follow different rules.

sentences.zh: 若人閑無役，地棄不墾，發閑人以耕棄地，省饋運以實軍糧，於是乎有屯田，其爲益多矣。

translations.literal: When men among the people have no corvée duties and land lies abandoned and unopened, then dispatching idle men to farm abandoned land and economizing on transport to fill military grain stores—that is when military colonies exist, and their benefit is great.
translations.idiomatic: When the people have no corvée to perform and land lies fallow, then sending idle men to open abandoned fields and saving transport costs to fill the army's granaries—that is what military colonies are for, and the gain is great.

sentences.zh: 今百官所退職田，散在諸縣，不可聚也。

translations.literal: Now the allotment fields relinquished by the hundred offices are scattered across the various counties and cannot be gathered together.
translations.idiomatic: The allotment fields now being returned by the hundred offices are scattered across many counties and cannot be assembled in one place.

sentences.zh: 百姓所有私田，皆力自耕墾，不可取也。

translations.literal: The private fields owned by the common people are all opened and cultivated by their own labor and cannot be taken.
translations.idiomatic: The private fields held by common people are all opened by their own labor and cannot simply be seized.

sentences.zh: 若置屯田，即須公私相換，征發丁夫，征役則業廢於家，免庸則賦闕於國。

translations.literal: If military colonies were established, it would require exchanging public and private holdings and conscripting laborers; if corvée were levied, livelihoods at home would be ruined, and if labor dues were waived, revenues owed to the state would fall short.
translations.idiomatic: To establish colonies here would require swapping public and private land and conscripting laborers. Levy corvée and households lose their livelihood; waive labor dues and the state's revenue falls short.

sentences.zh: 内地置屯，古所未有，得不補失，或恐未可。

translations.literal: Establishing colonies in the interior—something never before known in antiquity—might not repair the loss; it may perhaps not be feasible.
translations.idiomatic: Establishing colonies in the interior is unheard of in antiquity. The gain may not outweigh the loss, and I fear it cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 」其議遂止。

translations.literal: " The proposal thereupon ceased.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 先是，左庶子呉兢舊任史官，撰《唐書》一百巻、《唐春秋》三十巻，其書未成，以丁憂罷職。

translations.literal: Earlier, Left Household Mentor Wu Jing had formerly served as a historiographer and had compiled one hundred juan of the Book of Tang and thirty juan of the Annals of Tang, but the works were unfinished and he resigned his post to observe mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Left Household Mentor Wu Jing had served as a historiographer and had drafted one hundred juan of the Book of Tang and thirty juan of the Annals of Tang, but the works were unfinished when he left office to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 至是，上疎請終其功，有詔特令就集賢院修成其書。

translations.literal: At this point he submitted a memorial asking to complete the work, and an edict specially ordered him to finish the books at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: At this point he memorialized the throne asking to finish the work, and an edict specially ordered him to complete the books at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 及張説致仕，又令在家修史。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yue retired, he was again ordered to compile history at home.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yue retired, he too was ordered to compile history at home.

sentences.zh: 元紘奏曰：「國史者，記人君善惡，國政損益，一字褒貶，千載稱之，前賢所難，事匪容易。

translations.literal: Yuanhong memorialized, saying: "The national history records the sovereign's good and evil and the gain and loss of state policy; a single word of praise or blame is remembered for a thousand years. Former worthies found this difficult—it is no easy matter.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhong memorialized: "The national history records a ruler's good and evil and the gain and loss of state policy. One word of praise or blame is remembered for a thousand years. Former worthies found this hard—it is no light task.

sentences.zh: 今張説在家修史，呉兢又在集賢撰録，遂令國之大典，散在數處。

translations.literal: Now Zhang Yue is compiling history at home and Wu Jing is compiling and recording at the Hall of Assembled Worthies, so that the great statutes of the state are scattered in several places.
translations.idiomatic: Now Zhang Yue is compiling history at home while Wu Jing is drafting and recording at the Hall of Assembled Worthies, so the state's great canonical works are scattered in several places.

sentences.zh: 且太宗別置史館，在於禁中，所以重其職而秘其事也。

translations.literal: Moreover, Emperor Taizong specially established the Historiography Office inside the palace precincts in order to dignify the office and keep its affairs secret.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Emperor Taizong had specially established the Historiography Office within the palace precincts precisely to dignify the office and keep its work secret.

sentences.zh: 望勒説等就史館參詳撰録，則典冊有憑，舊章不墜矣。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will order Yue and the others to come to the Historiography Office to examine and compile in concert, so that the canonical books may have a fixed basis and old regulations not fall away.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Yue and the others be ordered to the Historiography Office to examine and compile together, so the canonical records have a fixed home and old regulations are not lost.

sentences.zh: 」從之，乃詔説及呉兢並就史館修撰。

translations.literal: " The proposal was accepted, and an edict ordered both Yue and Wu Jing to proceed to the Historiography Office to compile.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed and ordered both Yue and Wu Jing to the Historiography Office to compile.

sentences.zh: 元紘在政事累年，不改第宅，僕馬弊劣，未曾改飾，所得封物，皆散之親族。

translations.literal: Yuanhong served in the administration for many years without changing his residence; his servants and horses were worn and poor and were never refurbished, and whatever goods he received as enfeoffment he distributed among his kinsmen.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhong served in the administration for years without altering his house. His servants and horses were shabby and never replaced, and whatever he received as enfeoffment he gave away among his kin.

sentences.zh: 右丞相宋璟嘗嘉嘆之，毎謂人曰：「李侍郎引宋遙之美才，黜劉晃之貪冒，貴爲國相，家無儲積。

translations.literal: Right Chancellor Song Jing once praised and admired him, often telling people: "Vice Minister Li brought forward Song Yao's fine talent and dismissed Liu Huang's greed and presumption; though honored as a state minister, his household has no stored wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Right Chancellor Song Jing once praised him warmly, often saying to others: "Vice Minister Li advanced Song Yao's fine talent and removed Liu Huang for greed and presumption. Though he stands as a state minister, his house holds no store of wealth.

sentences.zh: 雖季文子之德，何以加也！

translations.literal: Even the virtue of Ji Wenzi—what could surpass it!
translations.idiomatic: Even the virtue of Ji Wenzi—what could surpass it!

sentences.zh: 」後與杜暹多所異同，情遂不叶，至有相執奏者，上不悅，由是罷知政事，出爲曹州刺史，以疾去官。

translations.literal: " Later he and Du Xian differed on many matters, and their feelings came to be at odds; they even submitted rival memorials to the throne. The emperor was displeased, and Yuanhong was therefore removed from the administration and sent out as governor of Cao Prefecture; he later resigned on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: " Later he and Du Xian clashed on many points until they no longer agreed, even submitting rival memorials to the throne. The emperor was displeased, Yuanhong was removed from the administration and sent out as governor of Cao Prefecture, and he later resigned because of illness.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜戸部尚書，仍聽致仕。

translations.literal: After some time he was appointed Minister of Revenue and allowed to retire.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed Minister of Revenue and permitted to retire.

sentences.zh: 二十一年疾瘳，起爲太子詹事，旬日而卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, when his illness had healed, he was recalled as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and died ten days later.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, when his illness had passed, he was recalled as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and died ten days later.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少傅，諡曰文忠。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous name Wenzhong ("Cultured and Loyal").
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous name Wenzhong, "Cultured and Loyal."

sentences.zh: 杜暹杜暹，濮州濮陽人也。

translations.literal: Du Xian—Du Xian was a native of Puyang in Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xian was a native of Puyang in Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父承誌，則天初爲監察御史。

translations.literal: His father Chengzhi, in the early reign of Empress Wu, served as Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chengzhi served as investigating censor in the early reign of Empress Wu.

sentences.zh: 時懷州刺史李文暕以皇枝近屬，爲讎人所告，承誌推出之。

translations.literal: At that time Li Wenlián, prefect of Huai Prefecture, a close kinsman of the imperial clan, was denounced by an enemy; Chengzhi investigated and cleared him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Wenlián, prefect of Huai Prefecture and a close kinsman of the imperial house, was denounced by an enemy. Chengzhi investigated and cleared him.

sentences.zh: 俄而文暕得罪，承誌坐貶，授方義令。

translations.literal: Before long Wenlián was found guilty, and Chengzhi was demoted and appointed magistrate of Fangyi.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wenlián was condemned, and Chengzhi was demoted and appointed magistrate of Fangyi.

sentences.zh: 累轉天官員外郎。

translations.literal: After successive promotions he became Outer Gentleman of the Celestial Office.
translations.idiomatic: After successive promotions he became outer gentleman of the Celestial Office.

sentences.zh: 既羅織事起，承誌恐懼，遂稱疾去官而歸，卒於家。

translations.literal: When the persecution of the "net fabrication" cases began, Chengzhi grew fearful, claimed illness, resigned, and returned home, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: When the fabricated "net" prosecutions began, Chengzhi grew afraid, claimed illness, resigned, and returned home, where he died.

sentences.zh: 自暹髙祖至暹，五代同居，暹尤恭謹，事繼母以孝聞。

translations.literal: From Xian's grand ancestor down to Xian, five generations lived together under one roof; Xian was especially respectful and cautious and was famed for serving his stepmother with filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: From Xian's great-grandfather down to Xian himself, five generations lived under one roof. Xian was especially respectful and cautious, and was known for serving his stepmother with filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 初舉明經，補婺州參軍，秩滿將歸，州吏以紙萬餘張以贈之，暹惟受一百，餘悉還之。

translations.literal: He first passed the Classics examination and was appointed military adjutant of Wu Prefecture. When his term ended and he was about to return home, the prefectural clerks presented him with more than ten thousand sheets of paper; Xian accepted only one hundred and returned all the rest.
translations.idiomatic: He first passed the Classics examination and was appointed military adjutant of Wu Prefecture. When his term ended and he was about to go home, the prefectural clerks gave him more than ten thousand sheets of paper as a parting gift. Xian accepted only one hundred and returned the rest.

sentences.zh: 時州僚別者，見而嘆曰：「昔淸吏受一大錢，復何異也！

translations.literal: At the time prefectural colleagues who were leaving saw this and sighed, "In olden days a pure official accepted one large coin—how is this any different!
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural colleagues who were leaving saw this and sighed, "In olden days a pure official accepted one large coin—how is this any different!

sentences.zh: 」俄授鄭尉，復以淸節見知。

translations.literal: " Shortly afterward he was appointed warden of Zheng County and again became known for his pure integrity.
translations.idiomatic: " Shortly afterward he was appointed warden of Zheng County and again won notice for his upright integrity.

sentences.zh: 華州司馬楊孚，公直士也，深賞重之。

translations.literal: Yang Fu, military administrator of Hua Prefecture, was an upright gentleman and held him in deep esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu, military administrator of Hua Prefecture, was an upright man and held him in deep esteem.

sentences.zh: 尋而孚遷大理正，暹坐公事下法司結罪，孚謂人曰：「若此尉得罪，則公淸之士何以勸矣？

translations.literal: Before long Fu was transferred to senior rectifier of the Court of Judicial Review. Xian was convicted of an official matter and tried in the judicial office. Fu said to people, "If this warden is punished, how are upright gentlemen to be encouraged?
translations.idiomatic: Before long Fu was transferred to senior rectifier of the Court of Judicial Review. Xian was convicted on an official matter and tried in the judicial office. Fu said to others, "If this warden is punished, how are upright men ever to be encouraged?

sentences.zh: 」特薦之於執政，由是擢拜大理評事。

translations.literal: " He specially recommended him to those in power, and Xian was thereupon elevated and appointed review official of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: " He specially recommended him to those in power, and Xian was thereupon promoted to review official of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 開元四年，遷監察御史，仍往磧西覆屯。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaiyuan he was transferred to Investigating Censor and was further sent to the Western Regions to re-examine the military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaiyuan he was made investigating censor and sent to the Western Regions to re-examine the military colonies.

sentences.zh: 會安西副都護郭虔瓘與西突厥可汗史獻、鎭守使劉遐慶等不葉，更相執奏，詔暹按其事實。

translations.literal: It happened that Vice Protector-General of Anxi Guo Qianjin was at odds with the Western Türk qaghan Shi Xian and Defense Commissioner Liu Xiaqing and others, each submitting rival memorials to the throne; an edict ordered Xian to investigate the facts of the case.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Vice Protector-General of Anxi Guo Qianjin was at odds with the Western Türk qaghan Shi Xian, Defense Commissioner Liu Xiaqing, and others, each submitting rival memorials to the throne. An edict ordered Xian to investigate the facts.

sentences.zh: 時暹已回至涼州，承詔復往磧西，因入突厥騎施，以究虔賫等犯狀。

translations.literal: By then Xian had already returned to Liang Prefecture; receiving the edict he went again to the Western Regions and entered the Turgish Türk territory to investigate the offenses of Qianjin and the others.
translations.idiomatic: By then Xian had already returned to Liang Prefecture. Receiving the edict, he went again to the Western Regions and entered Turgish Türk territory to investigate the offenses of Qianjin and the others.

sentences.zh: 蕃人賫金以遺，暹固辭不受。

translations.literal: A barbarian presented gold as a gift, and Xian firmly refused to accept it.
translations.idiomatic: A foreign envoy presented gold as a gift, and Xian firmly refused to accept it.

sentences.zh: 左右曰：「公遠使絶域，不可失蕃人情。

translations.literal: Those around him said, "You have come on a mission to a remote region—you cannot disregard the barbarians' goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: Those around him said, "You have come on a mission to a distant land—you cannot spurn the foreigners' goodwill.

sentences.zh: 」暹不得已受之，埋幕下，既去出境，乃移牒令收取之。

translations.literal: " Xian had no choice but to accept it, buried it beneath his tent, and after he left the border sent a dispatch ordering them to retrieve it.
translations.idiomatic: " Xian had no choice but to accept it, buried it beneath his tent, and after he had crossed the border sent a dispatch telling them to come and retrieve it.

sentences.zh: 蕃人大驚，度磧追之，不及而止。

translations.literal: The barbarians were greatly alarmed, crossed the desert in pursuit but could not overtake him and gave up.
translations.idiomatic: The foreigners were greatly alarmed, crossed the desert in pursuit, failed to overtake him, and gave up.

sentences.zh: 暹累遷給事中，丁繼母憂去職。

translations.literal: Xian was promoted in succession to Gentleman of the Rear Chancellery and resigned on account of mourning for his stepmother.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was promoted in succession to gentleman of the rear chancellery and left office to mourn his stepmother.

sentences.zh: 十二年，安西都護張孝嵩遷爲太原尹，或薦暹往使安西，蕃人伏其淸愼，深思慕之，乃奪情擢拜黃門侍郎，兼安西副大都護。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Protector-General of Anxi Zhang Xiaosong was transferred to be governor of Taiyuan. Some recommended Xian to go as envoy to Anxi; the barbarians respected his pure caution and deeply admired him. He was therefore recalled from mourning and elevated to Vice Director of the Yellow Gate and concurrently Vice Protector-General of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, Protector-General of Anxi Zhang Xiaosong was transferred to governor of Taiyuan. Some recommended Xian to serve in Anxi; the foreigners respected his upright caution and deeply admired him. He was therefore recalled from mourning, promoted to vice director of the Yellow Gate, and made concurrently vice protector-general of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 暹單騎赴職。

translations.literal: Xian traveled alone on horseback to take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Xian traveled alone on horseback to take up the post.

sentences.zh: 明年，於闐王尉遲眺陰結突厥及諸蕃國圖爲叛亂，暹密知其謀，發兵捕而斬之，並誅其黨與五十餘人，更立君長，於闐遂安。

translations.literal: The next year the king of Khotan, Yuchi Tiao, secretly allied with the Türks and various barbarian states to plot rebellion. Xian secretly learned of the plot, sent troops to capture and behead him, and also executed more than fifty of his partisans; a new ruler was installed, and Khotan was thereafter secure.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the king of Khotan, Yuchi Tiao, secretly allied with the Türks and various foreign states to plot rebellion. Xian learned of the plot in secret, sent troops to capture and behead him, and executed more than fifty of his followers. A new ruler was installed, and Khotan was secure.

sentences.zh: 暹以功特加光祿大夫。

translations.literal: For his achievement Xian was specially promoted to Glorious Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement Xian was specially promoted to Glorious Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 暹在安西四年，綏撫將士，不憚勤苦，甚得夷夏之心。

translations.literal: Xian spent four years in Anxi, comforting officers and soldiers and unafraid of hardship; he won the hearts of both barbarians and Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: Xian spent four years in Anxi, comforting officers and soldiers and unafraid of hardship, and won the hearts of both foreigners and Chinese.

sentences.zh: 十四年，詔暹同中書門下平章事，仍遣中使往迎之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year an edict appointed Xian co-signer of Secretariat-Chancellery documents, and a palace envoy was also dispatched to escort him back.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year an edict made Xian a co-signer of Secretariat-Chancellery documents and sent a palace envoy to escort him back.

sentences.zh: 及謁見，又賜絹二百匹、馬一匹、宅一區。

translations.literal: When he had audience, he was again granted two hundred bolts of silk, one horse, and one residence.
translations.idiomatic: When he had audience, he was again granted two hundred bolts of silk, one horse, and one residence.

sentences.zh: 後與李元紘不葉，罷知政事，出爲荊州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: Later he and Li Yuanhong were at odds; he was removed from the administration and sent out as chief administrator of the Great Protectorate of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he and Li Yuanhong fell out; he was removed from the administration and sent out as chief administrator of the Great Protectorate of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 又歴魏州刺史、太原尹。

translations.literal: He also served in succession as governor of Wei Prefecture and governor of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He also served in turn as governor of Wei Prefecture and governor of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 二十年，上幸北都，拜暹爲戸部尚書，便令扈從入京。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, when the emperor visited the Northern Capital, Xian was appointed Minister of Revenue and ordered at once to attend him on the return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, when the emperor visited the Northern Capital, Xian was appointed Minister of Revenue and ordered to accompany him back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 行幸東都，詔暹爲京留守。

translations.literal: On the imperial progress to the Eastern Capital, an edict appointed Xian as regent of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the imperial progress to the Eastern Capital, an edict appointed Xian regent of the capital.

sentences.zh: 暹因抽當番衞士，繕修三宮，增峻城隍，躬自巡檢，未嘗休懈。

translations.literal: Xian thereupon drew on the palace guards on rotation duty to repair the three palaces, raise and strengthen the city walls, and personally made the rounds of inspection, never slackening.
translations.idiomatic: Xian drew on the palace guards on rotation to repair the three palaces, raise and strengthen the city walls, and personally inspected the work, never slackening.

sentences.zh: 上聞而嘉之，賜敕書曰：「卿素以淸直，兼之勤幹。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of this he commended him and granted a written edict saying, "You have always been pure and upright, and moreover diligent and capable.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this he commended him and granted a written edict: "You have always been upright and pure, and moreover diligent and capable.

sentences.zh: 自委居守，毎事多能，政肅官僚，惠及黎庶。

translations.literal: Since I entrusted you with keeping the capital, you have been able in every matter; your government has disciplined the bureaucracy and brought benefit to the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Since I entrusted you with keeping the capital, you have been capable in every matter, disciplined the bureaucracy, and brought benefit to the people.

sentences.zh: 城隍宮室，隨事修營，且有成功，不疲人力。

translations.literal: City walls and palace halls you have repaired as occasion required, and with success, without exhausting human labor.
translations.idiomatic: You have repaired the walls and palace halls as occasion required, and with success, without exhausting the labor force.

sentences.zh: 甚善甚善，慰朕懷也。

translations.literal: Very good, very good—it puts my mind at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Very good, very good—it puts my mind at ease.

sentences.zh: 」俄代李林甫爲禮部尚書，累封魏縣侯。

translations.literal: " Shortly afterward he replaced Li Linfu as Minister of Rites and was enfeoffed in succession as Marquis of Wei County.
translations.idiomatic: " Shortly afterward he replaced Li Linfu as Minister of Rites and was enfeoffed in succession as Marquis of Wei County.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，病卒，年六十餘，詔贈尚書右丞相。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he died of illness at over sixty years of age; an edict posthumously granted him the title Right Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he died of illness at over sixty years of age. An edict posthumously granted him the title Right Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 暹在家孝友，愛撫異母弟昱甚厚。

translations.literal: At home Xian was filial and brotherly and treated his younger half-brother Yu with great affection.
translations.idiomatic: At home Xian was filial and brotherly and treated his younger half-brother Yu with great affection.

sentences.zh: 然素無學術，毎當朝談議，渉於淺近。

translations.literal: Yet he had never possessed learning, and whenever he joined court discussion his remarks tended toward the shallow and commonplace.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he had never possessed learning, and whenever he joined court discussion his remarks tended to be shallow and commonplace.

sentences.zh: 常以公淸勤儉爲己任，時亦矯情爲之。

translations.literal: He constantly took uprightness, purity, diligence, and frugality as his charge, though at times he also affected them.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly made uprightness, purity, diligence, and frugality his charge, though at times he also affected them.

sentences.zh: 弱冠便自誓不受親友贈遺，以終其身。

translations.literal: From early adulthood he swore that he would never accept gifts from relatives and friends throughout his life.
translations.idiomatic: From early adulthood he swore never to accept gifts from relatives and friends for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 及卒，上甚悼惜之，遣中使就家視其喪事，内出絹三百匹以賜之。

translations.literal: When he died the emperor greatly mourned him, sent a palace envoy to his home to oversee the funeral rites, and issued from the inner palace three hundred bolts of silk as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: When he died the emperor deeply mourned him, sent a palace envoy to his home to oversee the funeral, and issued from the inner palace three hundred bolts of silk as a gift.

sentences.zh: 尚書省及故吏賻贈者，其子孝友遵其素約，皆拒而不受。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue and former subordinates offered funeral gifts, but his son Xiaoyou, adhering to his father's lifelong pledge, refused them all.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue and former subordinates offered funeral gifts, but his son Xiaoyou, honoring his father's lifelong pledge, refused them all.

sentences.zh: 太常謚曰「貞肅」。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ceremonies proposed the posthumous name "Upright and Stern."
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ceremonies proposed the posthumous name "Upright and Stern."

sentences.zh: 右司員外郎劉同升、都官員外郎韋廉以暹有忠孝之美，所謚不盡其行，建議駁之。

translations.literal: Outer Gentleman of the Right Office Liu Tongsheng and Outer Gentleman of the Office of Punishments Wei Lian, holding that Xian possessed the excellence of loyalty and filial piety and that the proposed posthumous name did not exhaust his conduct, submitted a memorial of objection.
translations.idiomatic: Outer Gentleman of the Right Office Liu Tongsheng and Outer Gentleman of the Office of Punishments Wei Lian argued that Xian possessed the excellence of loyalty and filial piety and that the proposed posthumous name did not exhaust his conduct, and submitted a memorial of objection.

sentences.zh: 太常博士裴總執曰：「杜尚書往以墨缞受職事，雖云奉國，不得爲孝。

translations.literal: Erudite of the Minister of Ceremonies Pei Zong maintained, "When Vice Minister Du formerly accepted office while wearing mourning garb, though it was said to serve the state, it cannot count as filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite of the Minister of Ceremonies Pei Zong maintained: "When Vice Minister Du formerly accepted office while wearing mourning garb, though it was said to serve the state, it cannot count as filial piety.

sentences.zh: 請依舊爲定。

translations.literal: I ask that the original name be upheld.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the original name be upheld.

sentences.zh: 」孝友又詣闕陳訴上聞，而更令所司詳定，竟謚曰貞孝。

translations.literal: " Xiaoyou again went to the palace gate to petition the emperor, who heard of it and ordered the responsible office to examine and determine the matter; in the end the posthumous name was settled as "Upright and Filial."
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaoyou again went to the palace gate to petition the emperor. The emperor heard of it and ordered the responsible office to examine the matter again. In the end the posthumous name was settled as "Upright and Filial."

sentences.zh: 韓休韓休，京兆長安人。

translations.literal: Han Xiu—Han Xiu was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xiu was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 伯父大敏，則天初爲鳳閣舍人。

translations.literal: His father's elder brother Damin, in the early reign of Empress Wu, served as Secretariat Archivist.
translations.idiomatic: His father's elder brother Damin served as secretariat archivist in the early reign of Empress Wu.

sentences.zh: 時梁州都督李行褒爲部人誣告，云有逆謀，則天令大敏就州推究。

translations.literal: At that time Military Commissioner of Liang Prefecture Li Xingbao was falsely denounced by men of his department, who claimed he harbored treasonous designs; Empress Wu ordered Damin to go to the prefecture and investigate.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Military Commissioner of Liang Prefecture Li Xingbao was falsely denounced by men of his command, who claimed he harbored treasonous designs. Empress Wu ordered Damin to go to the prefecture and investigate.

sentences.zh: 或謂大敏曰：「行褒諸李近屬，太后意欲除之，忽若失旨，禍將不細，不可不爲身謀也。

translations.literal: Someone said to Damin, "Xingbao is a close kinsman of the Li clan; the Empress Dowager wishes to eliminate him. If you miss her intent, the disaster will be no small matter—you cannot fail to look out for yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to Damin, "Xingbao is a close kinsman of the Li clan. The Empress Dowager wishes to eliminate him. If you miss her intent, the disaster will be no small matter—you cannot fail to look out for yourself.

sentences.zh: 」大敏曰：「豈有求身之安而陷人非罪！

translations.literal: " Damin said, "How could one seek personal safety and yet frame another for a crime he did not commit!
translations.idiomatic: " Damin said, "How could one seek personal safety and yet frame another for a crime he did not commit!

sentences.zh: 」竟奏雪之。

translations.literal: " In the end he memorialized and cleared him.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end he memorialized and cleared him.

sentences.zh: 則天俄又命御史重覆，遂構成其罪，大敏坐推反失情，與知反不告同罪，賜死於家。

translations.literal: Empress Wu soon ordered censors to re-investigate; they then fabricated his guilt. Damin was convicted of erroneous judgment in a treason case, condemned under the same statute as one who knows of treason and does not report it, and was ordered to die at home.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu soon ordered censors to reinvestigate, and they fabricated his guilt. Damin was convicted of erroneous judgment in a treason case, condemned under the same statute as one who knows of treason and does not report it, and was ordered to die at home.

sentences.zh: 父大智，官至洛州司功。

translations.literal: His father Dazhi rose to the post of Record Keeper of Luo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dazhi rose to the post of record keeper of Luo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 休早有詞學，初應制舉，累授桃林丞。

translations.literal: Xiu early showed talent in letters; he first entered the palace examination and was appointed in succession as magistrate of Taolin.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu early showed talent in letters. He first entered the palace examination and was appointed in succession as magistrate of Taolin.

sentences.zh: 又舉賢良。

translations.literal: He also passed the "Exemplary and Good" examination.
translations.idiomatic: He also passed the "Exemplary and Good" examination.

sentences.zh: 玄宗時在春宮，親問國政，休對策與校書郎趙冬曦並爲乙第，擢授左補闕。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong was in the Eastern Palace he personally questioned the candidates on state affairs; Xiu's examination answer, together with that of collator Zhao Dongxi, both ranked in the second class, and he was elevated and appointed Left Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong was crown prince he personally questioned the candidates on state affairs. Xiu's examination answer, together with that of collator Zhao Dongxi, both ranked in the second class, and he was promoted to left remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 尋判主爵員外郎，歴遷中書舍人、禮部侍郎，兼知制誥，出爲虢州刺史。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was assigned as Outer Gentleman of the Directorate of Enfeoffment, and was promoted in succession to Secretariat Drafting Official and Vice Minister of Rites, concurrently drafting imperial edicts; he was then sent out as governor of Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was assigned as outer gentleman of the Directorate of Enfeoffment, promoted in succession to secretariat drafting official and vice minister of rites, concurrently drafting imperial edicts, and then sent out as governor of Guo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時虢州以地在兩京之間，駕在京及東都，並爲近州，常被支稅草以納閑廄。

translations.literal: At that time because Guo Prefecture lay between the two capitals, whenever the imperial carriage was at the capital or at the Eastern Capital it was counted among the nearby prefectures and was constantly called upon to supply fodder tax for the idle stables.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Guo Prefecture lay between the two capitals. Whenever the imperial carriage was at Chang'an or Luoyang it was counted among the nearby prefectures and was constantly levied for fodder tax to supply the idle stables.

sentences.zh: 休奏請均配餘州，中書令張説駁之曰：「若獨免虢州，即當移向他郡，牧守欲爲私惠，國體固不可依。

translations.literal: Xiu memorialized asking that the burden be evenly distributed among the remaining prefectures. Chief Minister Zhang Yue rejected it, saying, "If Guo Prefecture alone is exempted, the burden will simply shift to other commanderies; prefects and governors seeking to do personal favors—the body politic must not rely on that.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu memorialized asking that the burden be evenly distributed among the other prefectures. Chief Minister Zhang Yue rejected it, saying, "If Guo Prefecture alone is exempted, the burden will simply shift to other commanderies. Prefects and governors seeking to do personal favors—the body politic cannot rely on that.

sentences.zh: 」又下符不許之。

translations.literal: " An order was also sent down forbidding it.
translations.idiomatic: " An order was also sent down forbidding it.

sentences.zh: 休復將執奏，僚吏曰：「更奏必忤執政之意。

translations.literal: Xiu was about to persist in memorializing when his staff said, "If you memorialize again you will surely offend those in power.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu was about to persist in memorializing when his staff said, "If you memorialize again you will surely offend those in power.

sentences.zh: 」休曰：「爲刺史不能救百姓之弊，何以爲政！

translations.literal: " Xiu said, "As a prefect I cannot remedy the people's hardship—how can I govern!
translations.idiomatic: " Xiu said, "As a prefect I cannot remedy the people's hardship—how can I govern!

sentences.zh: 必以忤上得罪，所甘心也。

translations.literal: If I must offend my superiors and suffer punishment for it, I accept that willingly.
translations.idiomatic: If I must offend my superiors and suffer punishment for it, I accept that willingly.

sentences.zh: 」竟執奏獲免。

translations.literal: " He persisted in memorializing and obtained an exemption.
translations.idiomatic: He persisted in memorializing and obtained an exemption.

sentences.zh: 歳餘，以母艱去職，固陳誠乞終禮，制許之。

translations.literal: After a little more than a year, he left office on account of his mother's death, firmly stated his sincerity in begging to complete the mourning rites, and the emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: After a little more than a year he left office to mourn his mother, earnestly petitioned to complete the full mourning rites, and the emperor granted his request.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除工部侍郎，仍知制誥，遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was appointed Vice Minister of Works, still drafting imperial edicts, and was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, he was appointed vice minister of works, continued drafting imperial edicts, and was promoted to right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 開元二十一年，侍中裴光庭卒，上令蕭嵩舉朝賢以代光庭才，嵩盛稱休誌行，遂拜黃門侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Kaiyuan, Chief Minister Pei Guangting died. The emperor ordered Xiao Song to recommend worthy court officials to replace Guangting's talent. Song lavishly praised Xiu's character and conduct, and Xiu was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Chief Minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Kaiyuan, chief minister Pei Guangting died. The emperor ordered Xiao Song to recommend worthy officials to replace him. Song lavishly praised Xiu's character and conduct, and Xiu was appointed vice director of the Secretariat and concurrent chief minister.

sentences.zh: 休性方直，不務進趨，及拜，甚允當時之望。

translations.literal: Xiu's nature was upright and direct; he did not strive for advancement. When he was appointed, it greatly fulfilled the hopes of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu was upright by nature and did not court advancement. When he was appointed, the appointment greatly satisfied public expectation.

sentences.zh: 俄有萬年尉李美玉得罪，上特令流之嶺外，休進曰：「美玉卑位，所犯又非巨害，今朝廷有大姦，尚不能去，豈得舍大而取小也！

translations.literal: Soon the Wannian Assistant Commandant Li Meiyu committed an offense. The emperor specially ordered him exiled beyond the Ling Mountains. Xiu stepped forward and said, "Meiyu holds a low post, and his offense was not a great harm. Now the court has a great traitor whom it still cannot remove—how can it abandon the large and seize the small!
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Wannian assistant commandant Li Meiyu offended the law. The emperor specially ordered him exiled beyond the Ling Mountains. Xiu stepped forward and said, "Meiyu holds a low post and his offense was not grave. The court now has a great villain it still cannot remove—how can it let the great go and punish the small!

sentences.zh: 臣竊見金吾大將軍程伯獻，依恃恩寵，所在貪冒，第宅輿馬，僭擬過縱。

translations.literal: Your subject has privately observed the General of the Golden Guards Cheng Boxian, who relies on imperial favor, is everywhere greedy and corrupt, and in mansions, carriages, and horses exceeds proper limits with excessive indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: I have seen General of the Golden Guards Cheng Boxian rely on imperial favor to indulge greed wherever he goes—his mansions, carriages, and horses all exceed what his rank allows.

sentences.zh: 臣請先出伯獻而後罪美玉。

translations.literal: Your subject asks first to remove Boxian and afterward punish Meiyu.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Boxian be removed first and Meiyu punished afterward.

sentences.zh: 」上初不許之，休固爭曰：「美玉微細猶不容，伯獻巨猾豈得不問！

translations.literal: " The emperor at first would not agree. Xiu firmly contested, saying, "If even Meiyu's trivial offense cannot be tolerated, how can Boxian's great villainy go uninvestigated!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor at first refused. Xiu pressed his case: "If even Meiyu's petty offense cannot stand, how can Boxian's great villainy go uninvestigated!

sentences.zh: 陛下若不出伯獻，臣即不敢奉詔流美玉。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not remove Boxian, your subject dare not obey the edict to exile Meiyu.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does not remove Boxian, I dare not obey the edict to exile Meiyu.

sentences.zh: 」上以其切直，從之。

translations.literal: " Because of his blunt forthrightness, the emperor complied.
translations.idiomatic: " Impressed by his blunt honesty, the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 初，蕭嵩以休柔和易制，故薦引之。

translations.literal: At first Xiao Song considered Xiu gentle and soft and easy to control, and therefore recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: At first Xiao Song had considered Xiu gentle and easy to manage, and had recommended him for that reason.

sentences.zh: 休既知政事，多折正嵩，遂與休不葉。

translations.literal: Once Xiu took part in state affairs, he often corrected Xiao Song, and Song became incompatible with Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xiu entered government, he often corrected Xiao Song, and the two fell out.

sentences.zh: 宋璟聞之曰：「不謂韓休乃能如是，仁者之勇也。

translations.literal: Song Jing heard of it and said, "I never thought Han Xiu could act thus—it is the courage of a benevolent man.
translations.idiomatic: When Song Jing heard of it he said, "I never expected Han Xiu to act like this—the courage of a benevolent man.

sentences.zh: 其年夏，加銀靑光祿大夫。

translations.literal: That summer he was promoted to Silver-and-Blue-Green Glory Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: That summer he was promoted to Silver-and-Blue-Green Glory Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 十二月，轉工部尚書，罷知政事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he was transferred to Minister of Works and dismissed from participation in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he was transferred to minister of works and removed from the chief council.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，遷太子少師，封宜陽子。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred to Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and enfeoffed as Baron of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was made junior preceptor of the heir apparent and enfeoffed as Baron of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 二十七年病卒，年六十八，贈揚州大都督，謚曰文忠。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he died of illness at age sixty-eight. He was posthumously honored as Great Governor-General of Yang Prefecture, with the posthumous title Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he died of illness at sixty-eight. He was posthumously honored as great governor-general of Yang Prefecture, with the posthumous title Wenzhong (Cultured and Loyal).

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，重贈太子太師。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying he was again posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoying he was again posthumously honored as grand preceptor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 子洽、洪、汯、滉，皆有學尚，風韻髙雅。

translations.literal: His sons Qia, Hong, Yin, and Huang all had scholarly aspirations and refined, elegant bearing.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Qia, Hong, Yin, and Huang all pursued learning and carried themselves with refined elegance.

sentences.zh: 洽，天寶初爲殿中侍御史卒。

translations.literal: Qia served as Palace Censor in the early Tianbao era and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Qia served as palace censor in the early Tianbao era and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 洪，爲司庫員外郎。

translations.literal: Hong was Outer Gentleman of the Directorate of Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was outer gentleman of the Directorate of Granaries.

sentences.zh: 洽弟渾，除大理司直。

translations.literal: Qia's younger brother Hun was appointed Direct Clerk of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Qia's younger brother Hun was appointed direct clerk of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫王鉷犯法，籍沒其家，洽兄浩爲萬年主簿，捕其資財，有所容隱，爲京兆尹鮮于仲通所發，配流循州。

translations.literal: When Censor-in-Chief Wang Ang violated the law and his household was confiscated, Qia's elder brother Hao, chief clerk of Wannian County, seized his assets but concealed some; this was reported by Metropolitan Governor Xianyu Zhongtong, and Hao was sentenced to exile in Xun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When censor-in-chief Wang Ang broke the law and his property was confiscated, Qia's elder brother Hao, chief clerk of Wannian County, helped seize his assets but concealed part of them. Metropolitan governor Xianyu Zhongtong exposed this, and Hao was exiled to Xun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 洪、汯並坐貶職。

translations.literal: Hong and Yin were both demoted in rank for their association.
translations.idiomatic: Hong and Yin were both demoted for their association with the case.

sentences.zh: 後遇赦，量移洪爲華州長史。

translations.literal: Later, when an amnesty was granted, Hong was transferred by degree to Chief Administrator of Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when an amnesty was granted, Hong was transferred to chief administrator of Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 屬安祿山反，西京失守，洪陷於賊，賊授官，將見委任，洪與浩及汯、滉、渾同奔山谷，以投行在。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled and the Western Capital fell, Hong was trapped among the rebels; the rebels gave him an office and were about to entrust him with duties. Hong, together with Hao, Yin, Huang, and Hun, fled into the mountains and valleys to reach the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled and Chang'an fell, Hong was caught behind rebel lines. The rebels gave him an office and were about to entrust him with real duties. Hong fled with Hao, Yin, Huang, and Hun into the hills to reach the emperor's mobile court.

sentences.zh: 至谷口，洪、浩、渾及洪子四人並爲賊所擒，並命於通衢。

translations.literal: When they reached Gukou, Hong, Hao, Hun, and Hong's four sons were all captured by the rebels and executed in the public thoroughfare.
translations.idiomatic: At Gukou, Hong, Hao, Hun, and Hong's four sons were captured by the rebels and executed in the open road.

sentences.zh: 洪重交友，籍甚於時，見者掩涕，肅宗聞其重臣子，能以忠而死，贈太常卿。

translations.literal: Hong greatly valued friendship and was renowned in his time; those who witnessed it wiped away tears. Suzong heard that the son of a great minister had been able to die for loyalty and posthumously honored him as Chamberlain for Ceremonials.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was famed for his loyalty to friends, and those who saw his death wept openly. When Suzong heard that a great minister's son had died for loyalty, he posthumously honored Hong as chamberlain for ceremonials.

sentences.zh: 浩贈吏部郎中，渾贈太常少卿。

translations.literal: Hao was posthumously honored as Bureau Director of the Ministry of Personnel; Hun as Vice Chamberlain for Ceremonials.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was posthumously honored as bureau director of the Ministry of Personnel, and Hun as vice chamberlain for ceremonials.

sentences.zh: 汯，上元中爲諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Yin, during the Shangyuan era, served as Remonstrance Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Yin served as remonstrance grand master during the Shangyuan era.

sentences.zh: 滉、洄，別有傳。

translations.literal: Huang and Hui have separate biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Huang and Hui have separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 裴耀卿裴耀卿，贈戸部尚書守眞子也。

translations.literal: Pei Yaojing—Pei Yaojing, son of the posthumously honored Minister of Revenue Shouzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yaojing was the son of the posthumously honored minister of revenue Shouzhen.

sentences.zh: 少聰敏，數歳解屬文，童子舉。

translations.literal: From youth he was clever and quick; at several years old he could compose literary pieces, and he passed the child prodigy examination.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was clever; by several years of age he could compose essays and passed the child prodigy examination.

sentences.zh: 弱冠拜秘書正字，俄補相王府典簽。

translations.literal: At age twenty he was appointed Regular Scribe of the Secretariat; soon he was appointed Chief Registrar of the Prince of Xiang's household.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he was appointed regular scribe of the Secretariat; soon afterward he became chief registrar of the Prince of Xiang's household.

sentences.zh: 時睿宗在蕃，甚重之，令與掾丘悅、文學韋利器更直府中，以備顧問，府中稱爲學直。

translations.literal: At that time Ruizong was in his fief and greatly valued him. He was ordered to rotate duty in the princely household together with aide Qiu Yue and literary scholar Wei Liqi to serve as consultants; within the household they were called the Scholarly Duty Officers.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ruizong was still in his princely fief and valued him highly. He had Yaojing rotate duty in the household with aide Qiu Yue and literary scholar Wei Liqi as resident advisers; the household called them the Scholarly Duty Officers.

sentences.zh: 及睿宗升極，拜國子主簿。

translations.literal: When Ruizong ascended the throne, he was appointed Chief Clerk of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong took the throne, Yaojing was appointed chief clerk of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 開元初，累遷長安令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he was promoted in succession to magistrate of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he rose in succession to magistrate of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 長安舊有配戸和市之法，百姓苦之。

translations.literal: Chang'an long had a system of assigned households and government requisition markets, which the common people found burdensome.
translations.idiomatic: Chang'an had long used a system of assigned households and government requisition markets, and the people suffered under it.

sentences.zh: 耀卿到官，一切令出儲蓄之家，預給其直，遂無姦僦之弊，公私甚以爲便。

translations.literal: When Yaojing took office, he ordered that everything come from hoarding households, with payment given in advance, and thus there was no malfeasance in forced purchase; both public and private circles found it very convenient.
translations.idiomatic: When Yaojing took office, he required all supplies to come from households that kept stores, with payment made in advance. The abuses of forced purchase disappeared, and both officials and commoners found the change greatly convenient.

sentences.zh: 在職二年，寬猛得中。

translations.literal: In two years in office, leniency and severity were well balanced.
translations.idiomatic: In two years in office he balanced leniency and severity.

sentences.zh: 及去官，縣人甚思詠之。

translations.literal: When he left office, the county people greatly missed and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When he left office, the people of the county missed him and sang his praise.

sentences.zh: 十三年，爲濟州刺史。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was appointed governor of Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he became governor of Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其年，車駕東巡，州當大路，道里綿長，而戸口寡弱，耀卿躬自條理，科配得所。
