translations.literal: That year, when the imperial carriage toured east, the prefecture lay on the main road with a long stretch of route, while households were few and weak. Yaojing personally organized matters and apportioned levies appropriately.
translations.idiomatic: That year, when the emperor toured east, Ji Prefecture lay on the main route for a long stretch while its population was sparse and weak. Yaojing personally organized the work and apportioned levies fairly.

sentences.zh: 時大駕所歴凡十餘州，耀卿稱爲知頓之最。

translations.literal: At that time among the more than ten prefectures the imperial progress passed through, Yaojing was acclaimed as the best at provisioning the imperial halt.
translations.idiomatic: Among the more than ten prefectures the imperial progress passed through, Yaojing was acclaimed as the best at provisioning the imperial halt.

sentences.zh: 又歴宣、冀二州刺史，皆有善政，入爲戸部侍郎。

translations.literal: He also served successively as governor of Xuan and Ji Prefectures, all with good governance, and entered the capital as Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as governor of Xuan and Ji Prefectures, governing both well, and then entered the capital as vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 二十年，禮部尚書、信安王祎受詔討契丹，詔以耀卿爲副。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, Minister of Rites and Prince of Xin'an Li Shen received orders to campaign against the Khitan; the emperor ordered Yaojing as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, minister of rites and Prince of Xin'an Li Shen received orders to campaign against the Khitan, and Yaojing was appointed his deputy.

sentences.zh: 俄又令耀卿賫絹二十萬匹分賜立功奚官，就部落以給之。

translations.literal: Soon Yaojing was also ordered to carry two hundred thousand bolts of silk to distribute as rewards to Xi officials who had achieved merit, delivering the gifts at their tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yaojing was also ordered to carry two hundred thousand bolts of silk to reward meritorious Xi officials, delivering the gifts in their own camps.

sentences.zh: 耀卿謂人曰：「夷虜貪殘，見利忘義，今賫持財帛，深入寇境，不可不爲備也。

translations.literal: Yaojing said to others, "The barbarians are greedy and cruel; they see profit and forget righteousness. Now carrying wealth and silks deep into enemy territory, we cannot fail to take precautions.
translations.idiomatic: Yaojing told others, "Barbarians are greedy and cruel and forget righteousness at the sight of profit. Carrying wealth deep into enemy country, we cannot fail to take precautions.

sentences.zh: 」乃令先期而往，分道互進，一朝而給付並畢。

translations.literal: " He therefore had them go ahead of schedule, advance by separate routes in alternation, and within a single day all payments were completed.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent the payments ahead of schedule by separate routes, and within a single day all distributions were finished.

sentences.zh: 時突厥及室韋果勒兵邀險，謀劫襲之，比至而耀卿已還。

translations.literal: At that time the Turks and Shiwei indeed massed troops to block the passes and planned to rob and attack him; by the time they arrived, Yaojing had already returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks and Shiwei did indeed mass troops to ambush the passes and planned to rob him, but by the time they arrived Yaojing was already back.

sentences.zh: 其冬，遷京兆尹。

translations.literal: That winter he was transferred to Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was transferred to metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，霖雨害稼，京城穀貴。

translations.literal: The next autumn, incessant rain damaged the crops, and grain in the capital became expensive.
translations.idiomatic: The next autumn, heavy rains ruined the harvest and grain prices in the capital soared.

sentences.zh: 上將幸東都，獨召耀卿問救人之術，耀卿對曰：

translations.literal: The emperor was about to visit the Eastern Capital and summoned Yaojing alone to ask his method for saving the people. Yaojing replied:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to visit the Eastern Capital and summoned Yaojing alone to ask how the people might be saved. Yaojing replied:

sentences.zh: 臣聞前代聖王，亦時有憂害，更施惠澤，活國濟人，由是蒼生仰德，史冊書美。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that sage kings of former ages also at times suffered calamities, then applied further gracious benefits, reviving the state and aiding the people; thereby the common people looked up to their virtue, and historical records inscribed their praise.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that sage kings of former ages also suffered calamities at times, then extended further grace, reviving the state and saving the people. The common people looked up to their virtue, and history recorded their praise.

sentences.zh: 伏以陛下仁聖至深，憂勤庶政，小有饑乏，降情哀矜，躬親支計，救其危急。

translations.literal: I bow and consider that Your Majesty's benevolence and sagacity reach the deepest point; you worry and toil over common governance. At the slightest hunger and want you lower your feelings in pity and compassion, personally directing plans to rescue people in urgent peril.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's benevolence and sagacity run deep, and you toil over every branch of government. At the slightest hunger you show pity and personally direct relief to save people in urgent need.

sentences.zh: 上玄降鑒，當更延福祚，是因有小災而增輝聖德也。

translations.literal: High Heaven sends down its scrutiny; your fortune and eminence should be further extended—this is because a small disaster adds luster to sagely virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven watches over you, and your fortune should only grow—small disasters, met with grace, add luster to sagely virtue.

sentences.zh: 今既大駕東巡，百司扈從，太倉及三輔先所積貯，且隨見在發重臣分道賑給，計可支一二年。

translations.literal: Now that the imperial carriage already tours east and the hundred offices escort it, from the Grand Granary and the Three Adjuncts' prior stores dispatch senior officials at once by separate routes to distribute relief from what is on hand; it should suffice for one or two years.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the imperial carriage is touring east with the hundred offices in attendance, dispatch senior officials at once from the grand granary and the stores of the Three Adjuncts to distribute relief by separate routes from what is on hand. That should suffice for one or two years.

sentences.zh: 從東都更廣漕運，以實關輔。

translations.literal: From the Eastern Capital broaden transport by canal further to fill the Guan region.
translations.idiomatic: From the Eastern Capital, broaden canal transport to fill the Guan region.

sentences.zh: 待稍充實，車駕西還，即事無不濟。

translations.literal: When stores are somewhat replenished and the imperial carriage returns west, then nothing will fail to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Once stores are somewhat replenished and the imperial carriage returns west, nothing need fail.

sentences.zh: 臣以國家帝業，本在京師，萬國朝宗，百代不易之所。

translations.literal: Your subject considers that the empire's imperial enterprise has its root in the capital; all lands pay court there—it is a place unchanged for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: I believe the empire's foundation belongs in the capital, where all lands pay court—a seat that should not change for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 但爲秦中地狹，收粟不多，倘遇水旱，便即匱乏。

translations.literal: But because the Qin region's land is narrow and grain harvests are not large, if flood or drought occurs, stores are immediately depleted.
translations.idiomatic: But the Qin region is narrow and its harvests are small; if flood or drought strikes, supplies are quickly exhausted.

sentences.zh: 往者貞觀、永徽之際，祿稟數少，毎年轉運不過一二十萬石，所用便足，以此車駕久得安居。

translations.literal: Formerly during the Zhenguan and Yonghui eras, salary grain allotments were few; each year's transport did not exceed one or two hundred thousand shi—the amount used was sufficient, and by this the imperial carriage could long dwell in peace.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguan and Yonghui eras, salary grain allotments were smaller and annual transport did not exceed one or two hundred thousand shi—enough for daily needs, so the court could long remain settled in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 今國用漸廣，漕運數倍於前，支猶不給。

translations.literal: Now state expenditure gradually broadens; canal transport is several times what it was before, yet supply still does not suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Now state expenditure has grown, and canal transport is several times what it once was, yet supply still falls short.

sentences.zh: 陛下數幸東都，以就貯積，爲國大計，不憚劬勞，只爲憂人而行，豈是故欲不往。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has repeatedly visited the Eastern Capital to rely on stored reserves—it is a great plan for the state, not sparing arduous labor, going only out of concern for the people; surely you do not inherently wish not to go.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has repeatedly visited the Eastern Capital to rely on stored grain—a great plan for the state, undertaken without sparing labor, and driven only by concern for the people. Surely you do not wish to stay away by nature.

sentences.zh: 若能更廣陜運，支粟入京，倉稟常有三二年糧，即無憂水旱。

translations.literal: If transport through Shaan can be further broadened and grain supplied into the capital, granary stores constantly hold two or three years' grain—then there will be no worry about flood or drought.
translations.idiomatic: If transport through Shaan can be expanded and grain supplied into the capital so that granaries always hold two or three years' grain, there will be no fear of flood or drought.

sentences.zh: 今天下輸丁約有四百萬人，毎丁支出錢百文，五十文充營窖等用，貯納司農及河南府、陜州以充其費。

translations.literal: Today tax-paying males throughout the realm number roughly four million; each male pays one hundred cash, fifty for constructing granaries and the like, stored with the Directorate of Agriculture and the Henan Prefecture and Shaanzhou offices to meet the costs.
translations.idiomatic: Today tax-paying males throughout the realm number roughly four million. Let each pay one hundred cash, fifty of which would fund granary construction and the like, deposited with the Directorate of Agriculture and the offices of Henan Prefecture and Shaanzhou to meet the costs.

sentences.zh: 租米則各隨遠近，任自出腳送納東都。

translations.literal: As for rent grain, each pays according to distance and is free to pay transport costs to deliver it to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: As for rent grain, each locality should pay transport according to distance and deliver it to the Eastern Capital on its own account.

sentences.zh: 從都至陜，河路艱險，既用陸腳，無由廣致。

translations.literal: From the capital to Shaanzhou the river route is perilous; since land transport costs are used, it cannot be broadly supplied.
translations.idiomatic: From the capital to Shaanzhou the river route is perilous. Because land transport costs are used, large quantities cannot be moved.

sentences.zh: 若能開通河漕，變陸爲水，則所支有餘，動盈萬計。

translations.literal: If the river canal can be opened and transport changed from land to water, then expenditures will have surplus—amounting to tens of thousands at a stroke.
translations.idiomatic: If the river route can be opened and transport changed from land to water, costs would fall and savings would run into the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 且河南租船候水始進，呉人不便河漕，由是所在停留，日月既淹，遂生隱盜。

translations.literal: Moreover, Henan rent barges wait for water before advancing; Wu-region people are unsuited to canal transport, and so wherever they stop, as days and months drag on, concealed theft arises.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Henan rent barges wait for favorable water before advancing, and men from Wu are unused to canal transport. Wherever they stop, long delays breed concealed theft.

sentences.zh: 臣望沿流相次置倉。

translations.literal: Your subject proposes placing granaries in succession along the stream.
translations.idiomatic: I propose placing granaries in succession along the water route.

sentences.zh: 上深然其言。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor strongly approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 尋拜黃門侍郎、同中書門下平章事，充轉運使，語在《食貨志》。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Chief Minister, and served as Transport Commissioner; details are in the Monograph on Food and Commodities.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed vice director of the Secretariat and concurrent chief minister, and served as transport commissioner; details are recorded in the Monograph on Food and Commodities.

sentences.zh: 凡三年，運七百萬石，省腳錢三十萬貫。

translations.literal: In all three years he transported seven million shi and saved three hundred thousand strings in transport costs.
translations.idiomatic: Over three years he transported seven million shi of grain and saved three hundred thousand strings in transport costs.

sentences.zh: 或説耀卿請進所省腳錢，以明功利。

translations.literal: Some advised Yaojing to present the saved transport costs to display his achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Yaojing to present the saved transport costs to the throne to display his achievement.

sentences.zh: 耀卿曰：「此蓋公卿盈縮之利耳，不可以之求寵也。

translations.literal: Yaojing said, "This is merely the profit of surplus and deficit for the high officials—it cannot be used to seek favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yaojing said, "This is merely surplus profit for the high officials—it cannot be used to seek favor.

sentences.zh: 」乃奏充所司和市、和糴等錢。

translations.literal: " He then memorialized that it be applied to the office's funds for government purchase and proportional grain buying.
translations.idiomatic: " He then memorialized that the savings be applied to his office's funds for government purchase and proportional grain buying.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷侍中。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was promoted to chief minister.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，拜尚書左丞相，罷知政事，累封趙城侯。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was appointed Left Grand Counselor of the Department of State Affairs, dismissed from participation in state affairs, and cumulatively enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was appointed left grand counselor of the Department of State Affairs, removed from the chief council, and cumulatively enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhaocheng.

sentences.zh: 時夷州刺史楊浚犯贓處死，詔令杖六十，配流古州。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Jun, governor of Yi Prefecture, was condemned to death for corruption; an edict ordered sixty strokes of the rod and exile to Gu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yang Jun, governor of Yi Prefecture, was condemned to death for corruption; an edict ordered sixty strokes of the rod and exile to Gu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 耀卿上疎諫曰：

translations.literal: Yaojing submitted a memorial remonstrating:
translations.idiomatic: Yaojing submitted a memorial of remonstrance:

sentences.zh: 伏以聖恩天覆，仁育庶類，凡死罪之屬，不欲屍諸市朝，全其性命，流竄而已。

translations.literal: I bow and consider that sage grace covers like Heaven, nurturing all creatures in benevolence. All who fall under capital crimes—the court does not wish to expose their corpses in the marketplace; it preserves their lives and merely exiles them.
translations.idiomatic: Sage grace covers all like Heaven and nurtures every living thing in benevolence. For all who merit death, the court does not wish to expose their corpses in the marketplace—it preserves their lives and merely exiles them.

sentences.zh: 所以政致刑措，獄無冤人，曠古以來，未有斯美。

translations.literal: Therefore governance reaches the point where punishments are set aside and prisons hold no wronged persons—from remotest antiquity there has never been such beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this, government has reached the point where punishments lie unused and prisons hold no wronged persons—a beauty unmatched since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以爲全生免死，誠爲至化，有恥且格，爲訓將來。

translations.literal: Your subject in his foolishness considers that preserving life and sparing death is truly the highest transformation; shame and reform will serve as instruction for the future.
translations.idiomatic: I believe that preserving life and sparing death is the highest transformation, and that shame and reform will instruct generations to come.

sentences.zh: 茍有未安，不敢緘默。

translations.literal: If there is anything unsettling, I dare not keep silent.
translations.idiomatic: If anything here is amiss, I dare not keep silent.

sentences.zh: 臣以爲刺史、縣令，與諸吏稍別，人之父母，風化所瞻，一爲本部長官，即合終身致敬。

translations.literal: Your subject considers that prefects and county magistrates differ somewhat from other officials—they are parents to the people and exemplars of custom and transformation; once one becomes chief officer of a locality, people should show lifelong respect.
translations.idiomatic: I believe prefects and county magistrates differ from other officials—they are parents to the people and exemplars of custom. Once one becomes chief officer of a locality, the people owe him lifelong respect.

sentences.zh: 決杖者，五刑之末，只施於抶撲徒隸之間，官廕稍髙，即免鞭撻。

translations.literal: The deciding rod is the last of the five punishments; it is applied only among flogged servants and bondservants. When official privilege rank is slightly higher, whipping is waived.
translations.idiomatic: The deciding rod is the least of the five punishments and is applied only to bondservants and common laborers. Officials of even modest rank are exempt from whipping.

sentences.zh: 令決杖贖死，誠則已優，解體受笞，事頗爲辱。

translations.literal: Now to decide the rod in exchange for sparing death is truly already lenient, but to strip the body and receive beating is quite a disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: To commute death to the rod is already lenient, but to strip the body and receive beating is a grave disgrace.

sentences.zh: 法至於死，天下共之，刑至於辱，或有所恥。

translations.literal: When the law reaches death, all under Heaven share it; when punishment reaches disgrace, some may feel shame.
translations.idiomatic: When the law reaches death, all under Heaven share in it; when punishment reaches disgrace, some feel shame.

sentences.zh: 況本州刺史，百姓所崇，一朝對其人吏，背脊加杖，屈挫拘執，人或哀憐，忘其免死之恩，且有傷心之痛，恐非敬官長勸風俗之意。

translations.literal: Moreover, as governor of this prefecture he is revered by the common people; to have him once face his own subordinates, rods applied to his back, humiliated and bound—some may pity him, forget the grace of sparing his life, and feel a wound to the heart. I fear this is not the intent of honoring chief officers and encouraging custom.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, as governor he is revered by the people. To have him beaten before his own subordinates, bound and humiliated, may move some to pity and make them forget the grace of sparing his life, while the pain of the disgrace itself remains. I fear this is not how one honors chief officers and encourages proper custom.

sentences.zh: 又雜犯死罪，無杖刑，奏報三覆，然後行決。

translations.literal: Moreover, for miscellaneous capital offenses there is no rod punishment; the memorial is reported thrice for review, and only then is the sentence carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, for miscellaneous capital offenses there is no rod punishment; the memorial must be reviewed three times before the sentence is carried out.

sentences.zh: 今非時不覆，決杖便發，倘獄或未盡，又暑熱不耐，因杖或死，即是促其處分，不得順時。

translations.literal: Now at an improper season there is no triple review; the rod is decided and immediately applied. If the case is not yet complete, and moreover in unbearable summer heat one dies from the beating, this hastens the disposition and does not accord with the season.
translations.idiomatic: Now, at an improper season, there is no triple review and the rod is applied at once. If the case is not yet complete, or if the heat of summer proves unbearable and the beating itself causes death, the sentence is being rushed and does not accord with the season.

sentences.zh: 將欲生之，卻夭其命，又恐非聖明寬宥之意。

translations.literal: Wishing to preserve life yet cutting short their lives—I fear this is not the intent of sage clarity and clemency.
translations.idiomatic: Intending to preserve life yet cutting it short—I fear this is not the intent of sage clemency.

sentences.zh: 前後頻在州縣，或縁雜犯決人，毎大暑盛夏之時，決杖多死，秋冬已後，至有全者。

translations.literal: Having repeatedly served in prefectures and counties, when executing people for miscellaneous offenses, in the great heat of midsummer many died from the rod; after autumn and winter some survived whole.
translations.idiomatic: In my repeated service in prefectures and counties, when people were sentenced for miscellaneous offenses, many died from the rod in the great heat of midsummer; after autumn and winter some survived intact.

sentences.zh: 伏望凡刺史、縣令於本部決杖及夏暑生長之時，所定杖刑，並乞停減。

translations.literal: I bow and hope that whenever prefects and county magistrates decide the rod within their jurisdictions, and during the season of summer heat and growth, all rod punishments determined may be suspended or reduced.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask that whenever prefects and county magistrates decide the rod within their jurisdictions, and during the season of summer heat, all rod punishments be suspended or reduced.

sentences.zh: 即副陛下好生之德，於死者皆有再生之恩。

translations.literal: This would accord with Your Majesty's virtue of cherishing life; for those condemned to death it would all be a grace of renewed life.
translations.idiomatic: This would accord with Your Majesty's virtue of cherishing life and would be, for those condemned to death, a grace of renewed life.

sentences.zh: 俄而特進蓋嘉運破突騎施立功還，詔加河西、隴右兩節度使，仍令經略吐蕃。

translations.literal: Soon Vice Director of Attendants Gai Jiayun returned after defeating the Turgesh and achieving merit; an edict added him as military commissioner of both Hexi and Longyou, and also ordered him to strategize against Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Soon vice director of attendants Gai Jiayun returned after defeating the Turgesh with merit. An edict made him military commissioner of both Hexi and Longyou and ordered him to conduct strategy against Tibet.

sentences.zh: 嘉運既承恩寵，日夕酣宴，不時赴軍。

translations.literal: Jiayun, having received imperial favor, feasted and drank day and night and did not go to the army at the proper time.
translations.idiomatic: Having received imperial favor, Jiayun feasted and drank day and night and did not report to the army when he should.

sentences.zh: 耀卿密上疎曰：「伏見蓋嘉運立功破賊，更委兩軍，以勇果之才，承戰勝之勢，吐蕃小醜，不足殲夷。

translations.literal: Yaojing secretly submitted a memorial saying: "I have observed that Gai Jiayun has achieved merit in defeating bandits, and has further been entrusted with two armies; with his courageous and resolute talent, riding the momentum of victory, the small bandits of Tibet are not worth exterminating.
translations.idiomatic: Yaojing submitted a secret memorial: "I have observed that Gai Jiayun achieved merit by defeating the rebels and has been entrusted with command of two armies. With courageous, resolute talent and the momentum of victory behind him, the petty Tibetans are scarcely worth exterminating.

sentences.zh: 然臣近日與其同班，觀其舉措，精勁勇烈，誠則有餘，言氣矜誇，恐難成事。

translations.literal: Yet I have recently served with him on the same court schedule; observing his conduct, he is keen, vigorous, brave, and fierce—sincerity he has in surplus, but in speech and bearing he is proud and boastful; I fear he will hardly succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I have recently sat with him at court and watched his conduct. He is keen, fierce, and brave—sincerity he has in abundance—but his speech and bearing are proud and boastful. I fear he will find it hard to succeed.

sentences.zh: 莫敖敗於蒲騷之役，舉趾稍髙，《春秋》書之爲懲誡。

translations.literal: Mo Ao was defeated at the Battle of Pusao; he raised his step slightly high, and the Spring and Autumn records it as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: When Mo Ao was defeated at Pusao, he raised his step a little too high; the Spring and Autumn Annals recorded it as a warning.

sentences.zh: 恐其有驕敵之色，臣竊憂之。

translations.literal: I fear he has the look of one who treats the enemy lightly; I privately worry about this.
translations.idiomatic: I fear he shows the contempt of one who treats the enemy lightly, and I worry about it privately.

sentences.zh: 入秋防邊，日月稍逼，接對人吏，須識其宜。

translations.literal: As autumn approaches and border defense draws near, the days and months press closer; in receiving and dealing with personnel and officials, one must know what is appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: With autumn approaching and border defense imminent, time grows short. In meeting and managing staff and officials, one must know what is appropriate.

sentences.zh: 今將撫邊軍，未言發日，若臨事始去，人吏未識，雖決在一時，恐將非制勝萬全之道。

translations.literal: Now about to pacify the border armies, no departure date has been announced; if he only leaves when the matter arises, the people and officials will not know him. Though decisions may rest in a moment, I fear this will not be the way to ensure complete victory.
translations.idiomatic: He is about to take command of the border armies, yet no departure date has been set. If he waits until the crisis is upon him before leaving, his staff will not know him. Though decisions may rest in a moment, I fear this is not the way to secure a full victory.

sentences.zh: 況兵未訓練，不知禮法，人未懷惠，士未同心，求其忘性命於一時，憚嚴刑於少選，縱威逼而進，因而立功，恐非師出以律，久長之義。

translations.literal: Moreover, the troops are not yet trained and do not know ritual and law; the people have not received grace, and the soldiers are not of one mind. To expect them to forget life and death for a moment and fear severe punishment in a brief interval, to advance only by coercive force and thereby achieve merit—I fear this is not the meaning of troops departing in accordance with law, nor of enduring long-term policy.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the troops are untrained and ignorant of discipline; the people have not received kindness, and the soldiers are not united. To expect them momentarily to stake their lives while fearing harsh punishment only in the next breath, and to advance by coercion alone in hopes of merit—I fear this is not what is meant by sending troops forth in accordance with law, nor a policy built to last.

sentences.zh: 又萬人性命，決在將軍，不得已而行之，鑿兇門而即路。

translations.literal: Again, ten thousand lives depend on the general; when there is no choice but to proceed, one bores the Gate of Ill Omen and takes to the road.
translations.idiomatic: Again, tens of thousands of lives rest in the general's hands. When one has no choice but to proceed, one bores the Gate of Ill Omen and takes to the road.

sentences.zh: 今酣宴朝夕，優渥有餘，亦恐非愛人憂國之意，不可不察。

translations.literal: Now feasting merrily morning and evening, with generous favor in surplus—I fear this is not the intent of loving the people and worrying for the state; this cannot go unexamined.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now he feasts merrily morning and evening, enjoying lavish favor in abundance—a spirit, I fear, not of loving the people and worrying for the state. This cannot go unexamined.

sentences.zh: 若不可回換，即望速遣進途，仍乞聖恩，勗以嚴命。

translations.literal: If he cannot be replaced, I hope he may be quickly dispatched on his way; I still beg for sage grace and urge him with stern command.
translations.idiomatic: If he cannot be replaced, I hope he may be quickly sent on his way, and I beg that Your Majesty's grace may urge him with stern orders.

sentences.zh: 」疎奏，上乃促嘉運赴軍，竟以無功而還。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor then urged Jiayun to hasten to the army; in the end he returned without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor urged Jiayun to hurry to the army. In the end he returned without achievement.

sentences.zh: 天寶元年，改爲尚書右僕射，尋轉左僕射。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao, he was changed to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; soon he was transferred to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianbao he was made right vice director of the Department of State Affairs, and soon afterward was transferred to left vice director.

sentences.zh: 一歳薨，年六十三，贈太子太傅，謚曰文獻。

translations.literal: Within one year he died; he was sixty-three. He was posthumously granted Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, with posthumous title Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he died, aged sixty-three. He was posthumously granted grand mentor of the heir apparent, with the posthumous title Wenxian ("Cultural Contribution").

sentences.zh: 子綜，吏部郎中。

translations.literal: His son Zong was a bureau director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zong served as bureau director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 綜子佶。

translations.literal: Zong's son was Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Zong's son was Ji.

sentences.zh: 耀卿孫 佶佶，字弘正，幼能屬文。

translations.literal: Yaojing's grandson Ji Ji, styled Hongzheng, from youth could compose literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Yaojing's grandson Ji, styled Hongzheng, could compose literary pieces from childhood.

sentences.zh: 弱冠舉進士，補校書郎，判入髙等，授藍田尉。

translations.literal: At age twenty he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed collator, ranked in the upper grade in evaluation, and was granted the post of assistant magistrate of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: At age twenty he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed collator, ranked in the upper grade, and was made assistant magistrate of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 時有詔命畿内諸縣城奉天，時嚴郢爲京兆，政尚峻暴，加以朝旨甚迫，尹正之命，急如風霆。

translations.literal: At the time an edict ordered all counties within the capital region to fortify Fengtian. Yan Ying was then Grand Protector of Jingzhao; his governance favored severity and cruelty, and moreover the court's orders were very urgent—the commands of the chief prefect were swift as wind and thunder.
translations.idiomatic: At the time an edict ordered all counties around the capital to fortify Fengtian. Yan Ying was then grand protector of Jingzhao, and his rule was harsh and violent. Court orders pressed hard, and the chief prefect's commands fell like thunder.

sentences.zh: 本曹尉韋重規其室方娠而疾，畏郢之暴，不敢以事故免。

translations.literal: Wei Chonggui, assistant of the same bureau, whose wife was pregnant and ill, feared Yan's cruelty and did not dare request leave for the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chonggui of the same bureau had a pregnant, ill wife, but feared Yan's cruelty and did not dare request leave on that account.

sentences.zh: 佶因請代，役無愆程，當時義之。

translations.literal: Ji therefore requested to substitute for him; the service missed no deadline, and people at the time praised his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Ji therefore offered to take his place. The work missed no deadline, and contemporaries praised his conduct.

sentences.zh: 德宗南狩，佶詣行在，拜拾遺，轉補闕。

translations.literal: When Dezong went south on imperial hunt, Ji went to the temporary court, was appointed remonstrance official, and was then transferred to advisory censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong fled south, Ji went to the temporary court, was appointed remonstrance official, and was then made advisory censor.

sentences.zh: 李懷光以河中叛，朝廷欲以含垢爲意，佶抗議請討，上深器之，前席慰勉。

translations.literal: Li Huaiguang rebelled from Hezhong; the court wished to bear ignominy as policy. Ji protested and requested a campaign; the Emperor deeply valued him, moved forward on his mat and consoled and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Huaiguang rebelled at Hezhong, the court wished to swallow the insult. Ji protested and urged a punitive campaign. The Emperor thought highly of him, drew forward on his mat, and consoled and encouraged him.

sentences.zh: 三遷吏部員外，歴駕部兵部郎中，遷諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Three times promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Personnel; he served successively as bureau director in the Transport and War bureaus, and was promoted to remonstrance and debate grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted three times to vice director in the Ministry of Personnel, served successively as bureau director in the transport and war bureaus, and was promoted to remonstrance and debate grandee.

sentences.zh: 會黔中觀察使韋士宗慘酷馭下，爲夷獠所逐，俾佶代之，酋渠自化。

translations.literal: When observation commissioner Wei Shizong of Qianzhong was cruel in governing subordinates and was driven off by the Yi and Liao tribes, Ji was made to replace him, and the chieftains submitted of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When Qianzhong observation commissioner Wei Shizong ruled his subordinates with cruelty and was driven out by the frontier tribes, Ji was sent to replace him, and the chieftains submitted on their own.

sentences.zh: 其後爲瘴毒所侵，堅請入覲，拜同州刺史。

translations.literal: Afterward he was afflicted by miasmic poison; he firmly requested an audience at court and was appointed prefect of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was stricken by malarial illness. He repeatedly petitioned to return to court and was appointed prefect of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 征入爲中書舍人，遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Summoned to court as drafting officer of the Secretariat, he was promoted to right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court as a drafting officer of the Secretariat and was promoted to right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時兵部尚書李巽兼鹽鐵使，將以使局置於本行，經構已半，會佶拜命，堅執以爲不可，遂令徹之。

translations.literal: At the time Minister of War Li Xun also served as salt and iron commissioner and planned to place the commissioner's office within his own ministry; construction was already half complete. When Ji received his appointment, he firmly held it was not permissible and had it demolished.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Minister of War Li Xun also served as salt and iron commissioner and planned to place the commissioner's office within his own ministry; construction was already half finished. When Ji took office he firmly objected and had the work dismantled.

sentences.zh: 巽恃恩而強，時重佶之有守，就拜吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Xun relied on favor and was overbearing; the age respected Ji's integrity, and he was promptly appointed vice director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Xun traded on imperial favor and tried to force the issue, but the court respected Ji's steadfastness and promptly made him vice director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 以疾除國子祭酒，尋遷工部尚書致仕。

translations.literal: On account of illness he was appointed libationer of the Directorate of Education; soon he was promoted to Minister of Works and retired.
translations.idiomatic: Because of illness he was appointed libationer of the Directorate of Education, and soon was promoted to minister of works and retired.

sentences.zh: 元和八年卒，年六十二，贈吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yuanhe he died, aged sixty-two; he was posthumously granted Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yuanhe he died, aged sixty-two, and was posthumously granted minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 佶淸勁温敏，凡所定交，時稱爲第一流。

translations.literal: Ji was pure, forceful, warm, and quick; all with whom he formed friendships were at the time called first rank.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was clear-minded, forceful, warm, and quick-witted; all his close friends were counted among the finest men of the age.

sentences.zh: 與鄭餘慶特相友善，佶歿後，餘慶行朋友之服，搢紳美之。

translations.literal: He was especially friendly with Zheng Yuqing; after Ji's death, Yuqing wore mourning for a friend, and the gentry praised this.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially close to Zheng Yuqing. After Ji died, Yuqing wore the mourning of a friend, and courtiers praised the gesture.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰史臣曰：魏知古、盧懷愼、源乾曜、李元紘、杜暹、韓休、裴耀卿，悉蘊器能，咸居宰輔。

translations.literal: The historian says, the historian says: Wei Zhigu, Lu Huaishen, Yuan Ganyao, Li Yuanhong, Du Xian, Han Xiu, and Pei Yaojing—all possessed talent and capacity, and all served as chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Wei Zhigu, Lu Huaishen, Yuan Ganyao, Li Yuanhong, Du Xian, Han Xiu, and Pei Yaojing all possessed talent and all rose to chief minister.

sentences.zh: 或心存啓沃，或志在薦賢，或出愛子爲外官，或止屯田於關輔，或不受蕃人之賂，或堅劾伯獻之姦，或廣漕渠以充國用：此皆立事立功，有足嘉尚者也。

translations.literal: Some kept counsel in their hearts, some aimed to recommend the worthy, some sent beloved sons to posts outside the capital, some halted military colonies in the capital region, some refused bribes from the barbarians, some firmly impeached Boxian's wickedness, some expanded the canal to fill the state's needs—all these established affairs and achieved merit, worthy of praise and esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Some devoted themselves to counsel at court, some to recommending talent, some sent beloved sons to serve outside the capital, some halted military colonies in the Guanzhong region, some refused barbarian bribes, some firmly impeached Cheng Boxian's corruption, and some expanded the canals to enrich the treasury—all established their work and won merit truly worthy of praise.

sentences.zh: 盧、李、杜三君子，又以淸白垂美簡書，公孫弘之流也。

translations.literal: The three gentlemen Lu, Li, and Du further left their pure whiteness as beauty in the bamboo annals—the sort of Gongsun Hong.
translations.idiomatic: The three gentlemen Lu, Li, and Du further left reputations for integrity that grace the historical record—men in the mold of Gongsun Hong.

sentences.zh: 乾曜職當機密，無所是非，持祿保身，焉用彼相？

translations.literal: Ganyao's duty lay in state secrets; he had no judgments of right and wrong—holding salary and preserving himself; of what use was such a minister?
translations.idiomatic: Ganyao held a post at the heart of state secrets yet pronounced no judgments on right and wrong—he held his salary and preserved himself. What use was a minister like that?

sentences.zh: 贊贊曰：盧、魏、乾曜，弼違進賢。

translations.literal: The eulogy praises: Lu, Wei, and Ganyao—assisting with dissent and advancing the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy praises: Lu, Wei, and Ganyao, who assisted through dissent and advanced worthy men.

sentences.zh: 裴、韓、李、杜，遠財劾姦。

translations.literal: Pei, Han, Li, and Du—keeping wealth at a distance and impeaching wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Pei, Han, Li, and Du kept wealth at arm's length and impeached corruption.

sentences.zh: 汗簡書事，淸風肅然。

translations.literal: Bamboo annals inscribe the affairs; pure wind stands solemn.
translations.idiomatic: Recorded in the bamboo annals, their integrity stands solemn and clear.

sentences.zh: 萬歳之後，其名不刊。

translations.literal: After ten thousand years, their names will not be effaced.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand years hence, their names will endure undiminished.
